_about: cuttle agent-experience session audit, 2026-08-04..2026-08-18. Anonymized: session labels S01..S46, sites replaced with category descriptions. See docs/researches/2608-18-cuttle-issues-and-improvements-research.md
corpus_stats: Window 2026-08-04..2026-08-18 (14 days), verified by SQL over the session store rather than taken from the upstream clusters. 627 sessions created in the window, of which 188 are root (non-subagent) sessions. 114 sessions issued a cuttle or driver command - 50 root + 64 subagent - which is the correction to the upstream `sessions_affected` figures: those counts silently mixed subagents and roots (S16 plus its four `S16/agent-*` audits are one investigation, not five sessions). 72 sessions actually drove pages. Command volume in the window: 2749 driver invocations (playwright-cli / agent-browser / browser-use), 1337 cuttle CLI invocations, 968 eval/run-code calls, 592 snapshot calls, 661 browser calls carrying a literal `sleep`, 185 synthetic-click calls (`dispatchEvent` / `.click()`) across 21 sessions, 113 driver screenshots total with 55 of the 72 page-driving sessions (76%) taking zero and one session taking 22. cuttle's own verb usage over the same window: `cuttle up` 37, `cuttle downloads` 44, `cuttle status` 25, `cuttle --context` 13, `cuttle skill` 5, `cuttle open` 2, `cuttle context` 1. Inputs to this ranking: 63 clustered issues from the upstream passes plus 10 finding-classes the critics showed were dropped in clustering; after merging mechanically-identical clusters and splitting three over-merges, 38 distinct issues below. Source spot-checks against the tree at 6b2a4bf (0.11.4) confirmed the load-bearing mechanics cited: humanize.go constants `methodMouse`/`methodKey`/`methodInsertText` (the humanizer sits on exactly three CDP methods), `insertTextMaxRunes = 80` at humanize.go:156 with the silent bypass at humanize.go:592, and `Page.createIsolatedWorld` at humanize.go:1036 (the main-world probe leak is genuinely fixed in this build).

ranked_issues.issue: No write in the stack returns a post-condition: clicks, fills and saves report success while changing nothing, so every session hand-builds a bespoke verification loop after every mutation
ranked_issues.frequency: 16 sessions; the single largest call-cost class in the corpus - S01 spent ~400 of 892 calls (46%) answering 'what is actually on the page'
ranked_issues.evidence: S01 built an out-of-band protocol - Gravar -> `cuttle downloads` -> grep the form XML - after every single field, because 'Q6 is confirmed still empty in the XML (the click didn't take - custom widget)', and downloaded the same file nine times tracking Chrome's `(3).xml`..`(9).xml` dedup counter by hand. S05: `el.click()` on Google's account chooser returned 'clicked account' with the URL unmoved; a bash loop over freshly-snapshotted refs printed three empty arrows and added zero pages while looking like it ran. S09: a hosting provider Submit no-op'd through three clicks and two full form refills. Corpus-wide 592 snapshot calls against 2749 driver calls - roughly one page re-read per four actions, almost all of it read-back.
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle already computes a settle gate and an aria-toggle post-click verify internally for humanized clicks and discards the verdict; fill/type have no equivalent at all; drivers exit 0 on no-ops. Note this issue covers only the two mechanical cases the daemon can see - input never dispatched, and input dispatched but ignored by the page. The third case the upstream cluster merged in (an HTTP 200 that discarded the write) is mechanically unrelated and is ranked separately at #14.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Every cuttle-owned write returns the post-condition instead of a checkmark: 'click landed at (x,y) on <el>, DOM subtree changed / unchanged, active element after = <sel>, field value before -> after, N requests failed'. Extend the existing humanized-click verify to fill/type and surface the verdict the daemon already computes.

ranked_issues.issue: Input dispatched to a non-foreground tab is silently swallowed and background tabs get near-zero rAF, so actionability never settles and lazy loaders never fire - one root cause that wore four different disguises for two weeks
ranked_issues.frequency: 7 sessions; 139 timeout-signature results = 4.9% of 2827 browser calls in S16's measured window, and 0 of 8 identical retries ever worked
ranked_issues.evidence: S16 measured it on live containers: 'noDefaults:true G/background -> fps 0, click FAIL 15002ms (waiting for element to be visible, enabled and stable)' vs 'noDefaults:false G/background -> fps 61, click OK 851ms'. S05 rediscovered 'The tab is backgrounded (visibilityState: hidden), so Google's UI won't respond' at least four separate times. S02 spent 58 calls concluding 'cuttle's Chromium never fires the lazy RSC requests', told the user 'I have to stop and hand this back to you', then twenty minutes later: 'Found it - document.hidden === true... That was the whole bug - a background tab, not a cuttle limitation.'
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle's base Chrome args omit Playwright's four backgrounding switches, and the connectOverCDP/noDefaults:true attach path cuttle documents skips Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled. The per-page pin shipped in 0.11.4 restores compositing but does not make document.visibilityState 'visible', so IntersectionObserver lazy loaders still never fire and long-hidden tabs still degrade to ~1fps.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Extend the pin to page-visibility, pass the renderer anti-backgrounding launch flags, expose per-target foreground/visibilityState in `cuttle status`, and error when Input is dispatched at a target that cannot receive it instead of dropping it silently.

ranked_issues.issue: When the driver's click fails there is no trusted-click escape hatch, so agents escalate to force-click, DOM dispatchEvent and hand-computed coordinates - the exact move that emits isTrusted:false and throws away the product's only reason to exist
ranked_issues.frequency: 185 synthetic-click calls across 21 sessions in the 14-day window (verified by SQL), against 968 eval/run-code calls total
ranked_issues.evidence: S07 caught itself: 'synthetic events are isTrusted: false, while cuttle's humanized input layer sends real CDP input events... Making dispatchEvent my reflex quietly throws away the stealth property on exactly the anti-bot sites where we need it.' S05 rebuilt clicking from scratch - 27 evals whose only job was getBoundingClientRect, each followed by `mousemove X Y; mousedown; mouseup`, coordinates stale on any reflow - and then proved the cost: `el.click()` on Google's account chooser reported success with the URL unmoved, and only a real mouse press advanced it. S09: 'roughly 30 of the 64 driver calls are --raw eval DOM surgery, including every Submit click'. S13 pressed a Save button with an injected `b.click()` because no ref existed.
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle's humanized input is reachable only through a driver verb that frequently cannot resolve or act on the element (see #2, #4, #22), and cuttle offers no native alternative - so the only available escape hatch is the one that defeats humanization. The daemon cannot even see it happen: the humanizer sits on Input.dispatchMouseEvent / dispatchKeyEvent / insertText (humanize.go:136-138) and anything through Runtime.evaluate is invisible to it.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle click <selector|x,y>` that resolves, scrolls into view, foregrounds the target and dispatches humanized real Input in one call; plus a hard SKILL.md rule that dispatchEvent/force-click through cuttle is forbidden, paired with that alternative so the rule is followable.

ranked_issues.issue: The accessibility snapshot omits or mislabels exactly the controls real authenticated apps use (Save buttons, OAuth links, expanders, Angular, LWC, legacy WebForms and shadow-DOM widgets), so raw-JS DOM extraction became the universal escape hatch
ranked_issues.frequency: 10 sessions; the most-repeated workaround in the corpus and the direct upstream cause of #3
ranked_issues.evidence: S13: `snapshot | rg -i 'button.*save|publish|Save'` returned only 'Published on June 30, 2022'; a raw eval over document.querySelectorAll('button') found ' Save'. S14: ~20 of ~35 a consumer banking web app calls were raw evals because the a11y layer was useless on legacy WebForms. S07: 'The form lives in a CRM platform LWC shadow DOM - document.querySelector can't see it (Playwright locators can)' - the agent hand-wrote a shadowRoot walker. S15: `find 'Continue with GitHub' | rg 'ref='` returned four nested generics and no link ref.
ranked_issues.root_cause: The a11y tree is the only structured page view cuttle's documented drivers offer and it is lossy on the widget families that matter. There is no blessed structured-extraction path, so agents fall to page-context JS - which is blind to shadow DOM and bypasses humanization.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle extract --selector ... --format json` returning form values keyed by nearest stable id/name/label, piercing shadow DOM and spanning frames; plus a documented rule that eval is for reads only and that locators pierce shadow DOM where document.querySelector does not.

ranked_issues.issue: Multiple clients share one browser with no visibility, ownership or lease - a human or a second agent silently clobbers the agent's work, and the surfaced error always blames the selector
ranked_issues.frequency: 7 sessions observed; true base rate unknowable (see blind spot 8) - the one caught pair was caught only because both narrated confusion in the same minute
ranked_issues.evidence: S05 and S06 ran against the SAME container simultaneously on 2026-08-07 and were each other's invisible saboteur. S05: 'Stopping here - we're both driving the same browser and it's clobbering the work... That also explains the three Create connection clicks that did nothing' - task handed back to the human, the corpus's only user interrupt. S06: 'another session has opened tabs in this browser and stolen document focus, which makes execCommand a no-op' - after it had already corrupted a live build config into `[v0.14.6 array][v0.14.5 array]`. S12 found the deployment-scale version: local dev and prod compute the same deterministic seed and land on the same single-replica Chrome, 'either side's browser.close() can kill the other's page'.
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle multiplexes CDP but exposes no notion of who else is attached or which targets are claimed; seeds are a small deterministic pool with no per-client namespacing; `cuttle status` says nothing about attached clients. cuttle's own `--context` feature is the fix and was used once corpus-wide.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Per-attach target ownership or an advisory lease, attached-client count and foreground owner in `cuttle status`, per-client seed namespacing, and a briefing line telling an agent to claim a context when another session may be driving.

ranked_issues.issue: Discoverability, not capability, is the binding constraint: shipped affordances that exactly solve top-ranked problems went essentially unused, so the corpus's apparent demand for ~25 new verbs is partly a demand for a findable briefing
ranked_issues.frequency: Corpus-wide. Verified usage in the window: `cuttle up` 37 calls but `cuttle open` 2, `cuttle skill` 5, `--context` 13 (concentrated in dev/audit sessions), `cuttle context` 1. run-code was used 201 times but in only 19 of 72 page-driving sessions
ranked_issues.evidence: `--context` / `context ls|add` is the exact fix for the #5 collision incident, is never mentioned in the `cuttle up` briefing, and was reached for once in 14 days. S05 read the driver's own SKILL.md documenting run-code and made zero run-code calls in 183 browser calls; its own audit put ~65 of those as collapsible to ~5. S07 on agent-browser batch: 'That's the thing I claimed was structural.' S28 truncated the `cuttle up` briefing to `tail -2` to save context, discarding the routing rules entirely. S01 opened a non-cuttle browser for a second identity and the user had to ask 'are you using cuttle? or some magic stuff yourslef?' before it learned `cuttle up --name` exists.
ranked_issues.root_cause: The briefing teaches attachment and names drivers; it does not name the features that resolve the failures agents actually hit, and it is long enough that agents truncate it. Any remedy list read off this corpus will over-weight new verbs because a missing verb and an unfindable verb are indistinguishable in a transcript.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: A short, stable `cuttle up` briefing (short enough that nobody truncates it) that names the existing escape hatches against the symptoms that trigger them - second identity -> `cuttle up --name`, another driver present -> `--context`, slow discrete loop -> run-code/batch, bulk entry on your own account -> `--humanize=false` - with the full guide behind `cuttle skill`.

ranked_issues.issue: The operational facts that decide success live nowhere durable, so every session re-derives the same mechanics and then writes a private cuttle playbook into the user's own repo - and cuttle's embedded SKILL.md carries claims that are factually false about the daemon
ranked_issues.frequency: 11 sessions re-deriving; 3 sessions acting on false SKILL.md claims; three different user repos now carry hand-rolled cuttle documentation
ranked_issues.evidence: The same four driver mechanics were independently re-derived in at least five sessions: run-code is Node not the page, run-code needs an `async page => {}` wrapper, long text needs insertText, click sometimes needs raw coordinates. S10 wrote them into `pjs/career/docs/SCAM_REPORTING.md` under 'Driving these forms with cuttle'; S01 wrote a 34-line block into `pjs/finances/CLAUDE.md`; S02 rewrote `tools/a professional social network-access/CLAUDE.md`. The humans said it directly: 'have you checked full skills/docs of both tools? could it be that we are just not using them in the most efficient way?' (S07 - the agent's own answer: 'Roughly 12-15 of my ~30 browser calls were avoidable'). On the false-claims half, S16: 'internal/cli/SKILL.md:200 claims off-centre clicks (the code removed that at humanize.go:398-403), and it says typing is rewritten into human-paced motion when fill on both drivers goes through Input.insertText, which the humanizer never sees.'
ranked_issues.root_cause: SKILL.md is //go:embed'ed and is therefore shipped behaviour, but nothing keeps its behavioural claims under test against the daemon's code paths, and the load-bearing operational rules are carried by neither the briefing nor SKILL.md.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Move the handful of load-bearing rules into the embedded SKILL.md, and add a test asserting SKILL.md's behavioural claims against the daemon (keystroke counts on fill, click offsets, flag pass-through) so docs drift cannot land silently.

ranked_issues.issue: There is no wait-for-condition primitive, so agents pad every action with blind sleeps and hand-roll polling loops, and 'is it stuck or just slow' is never answerable
ranked_issues.frequency: 661 browser calls in the window carry a literal sleep (verified); 14 sessions; >1 hour of pure wall clock, one session at 58% of calls
ranked_issues.evidence: S06: 32 sleeps totalling 894s plus 7 hand-rolled polling loops (~40 min), including `for i in 1..8; do sleep 40; playwright-cli goto ".../tests/<id>?p=$i"`, and one attempt rejected by the harness ('Blocked: sleep 150 followed by: curl'). S05: 85 of 183 browser calls contain a sleep, 354s total. S04: 76 sleeps (~264s) despite SKILL.md's own rule 'Never sleep; wait for a condition' - because it had navigated inside eval, leaving no driver-side navigation to wait on.
ranked_issues.root_cause: No wait primitive at the cuttle layer and no confidence in the drivers'; combined with humanized latency and cold starts, agents cannot distinguish designed slowness from a hang, so they guess a duration on every interaction. Several sessions also appended cache-busting query params because there is no hard-reload verb.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle wait --tab N --until '<js predicate>' | --url-matches | --settled --timeout`, a documented hard reload, and a stated per-action latency budget so agents stop padding a humanized click with a 9-second sleep.

ranked_issues.issue: The dominant real use of cuttle is authenticated data extraction through a tab that carries the user's cookies, and it has no verb - so every session reverse-engineers the site's private API and re-derives its auth flow from scratch
ranked_issues.frequency: 15 sessions; in three of them (S36, S37, S40) not one CDP input event was ever sent - zero clicks, zero typing
ranked_issues.evidence: The identical incantation appears in S23, S37, S29, S33, S27 and S34: `--raw eval "async () => { const t=(await (await fetch('https://api.a freelance marketplace/auth/refresh-token',{method:'POST',credentials:'include'})).json()).token; ... }" | jq`. S17 spent 24 of 29 calls on in-page fetch of a link-aggregator site .json because 'plain curl is bot-blocked', carrying a 400-character shell-quoted blob as session state across three compactions. S02's user pushed back directly: 'every time i ask you to check a professional social network, do you need to run cuttle for that? could you store the token in here somehow?'
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle's value today is 'a logged-in cookie jar reachable over CDP', and the briefing names drivers and attach commands but never names this use case, so everything above that layer is the agent's own JS re-derived per session and per site.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle fetch <url> [--json] [--out file]` and `cuttle eval --file script.js` executing in the seed's authenticated page context, returning un-escaped output and streaming large results to a file. The most-used capability in the batch and the only one with no verb.

ranked_issues.issue: Agents have no cheap visual ground truth and no rule for when to look, and the one capture path they do have is unreliable - so page-state questions get answered from DOM reads that lie, while the sessions that do screenshot mostly waste them
ranked_issues.frequency: 55 of 72 page-driving sessions (76%) took zero driver screenshots; 113 total in the window, 22 of them in a single session that its own audit calls pure waste; 6 sessions hit hard capture failures
ranked_issues.evidence: S01: 628 driver calls broke down as snapshot 245, eval 208, click 69, screenshot 6, and the user finally asked 'are you able to screenshot the whole page so that you won't be guessing so much missing stuff from what is actually on screen?' then caught a wrong tax figure himself ('and check the screenshot, you did some shit' - campo 61 read 9.819,81). S05: zero screenshots in 183 calls, 27 evals whose only job was getBoundingClientRect. S17: zero screenshots in 29 calls while the human pasted [Image #1]-[Image #12]. On the reliability half, S04 hit three identical 'TimeoutError: Timeout 5000ms exceeded... taking page screenshot - waiting for fonts to load' on three unrelated sites and then abandoned visual verification for the session; S22's capture printed 'ok' and wrote no file; S09 used `--path=` (the flag is `--filename`) and got three byte-identical 251.9K PNGs of a virtualized list; S08 needed `--hires` plus a hand-written PIL 5x upscale to read a 140x60 captcha.
ranked_issues.root_cause: Two coupled defects. cuttle has no capture of its own, so visual truth is inherited driver behaviour whose page-screenshot path waits on document.fonts.ready - which does not settle in cuttle's container, almost certainly because of the metric-renamed win/mac font packs the image installs. And nothing anywhere states when an image is the cheapest answer, so the distribution is bimodal: most sessions never look, one session looks reflexively and learns nothing.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: A daemon-side capture (CDP Page.captureScreenshot with clip + deviceScaleFactor, no font gate) echoing an absolute path and a content hash, exposed as `cuttle shot [--tab N] [--full] [--element sel]`; plus a SKILL.md decision rule naming the four situations where an image is the cheapest answer (two consecutive no-op actions, an icon-only control, a control that reports enabled but does nothing, any visual-judgment request) and the one where it is not (routine state read - use a scoped text extract).

ranked_issues.issue: Tabs are addressed by positional integer in a browser other actors freely mutate, with no agent-owned tab, no stable handle and no cuttle tab verb at all
ranked_issues.frequency: 16 sessions; one audit counted ~115 calls corpus-wide, and one session spent 33 calls (18%) purely on tab orientation
ranked_issues.evidence: S17: an eval landed on the human's own tab and returned `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<', "<!doctype "... is not valid JSON` - twice - and the compaction summary had to carry 'my tab is tab 1, tab 0 is HIS' as standing state, which inverted when the human closed a tab. S15: `tab-close 3; tab-close 1; tab-close 0` in one command left four tabs with reshuffled indices. S05: an eval intended for a Notion dialog executed against a a SaaS console page and returned a React stack trace the agent did not recognise as wrong-page output. Aggravated by attach hygiene: S27 attached onto `0: (current) [](https://a media-index site/signup.php)` and auto-snapshotted it; S15 attached into a browser holding `0: [Logout - a consumer banking web app](.../a session-timeout page)` and `3: [a consumer banking app](https://a consumer banking web app/logged-out)`.
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle exposes no tab/target concept - enumeration arrives only as a driver side effect, indices are positional, cuttle's own immortal keep-alive about:blank occupies an ordinal that shifts everything after it, and attach binds to whatever page the last human or agent left focused.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle open --name <label>` returning a stable target id, `cuttle tabs` listing id/url/title/foreground/owner, driver commands pinnable to an id (or an `--expect-url` guard that fails rather than executing against whatever is at that ordinal now), and a dedicated working tab handed to each attaching client.

ranked_issues.issue: Native JS dialogs are invisible to the agent and unowned by cuttle: commands stall silently behind a pending dialog, accepting one destroys unsaved client-side state with no warning, and a dialog held by one driver wedges the tab for every other client
ranked_issues.frequency: 3 sessions, 6 episodes - but each episode is catastrophic rather than costly, and dialogs are per-driver-session so cross-client wedges cannot be counted
ranked_issues.evidence: S01: four separate 'Leave site?' episodes on a completed tax declaration; 'The draft is still alive - the navigation is stuck on the pending dialog' followed later by 'The navigation had already fired, so the in-browser draft is gone'; the user: 'can you do those changes without reuploading the file now? i'm tired of you getting stuck on Leave site? screens'. Only 4 dialog-accept and 1 dialog-dismiss calls exist in the whole 892-call session - every other dialog was discovered by inference after commands stopped working. S02, mid-task driver switch: 't2 is stuck - likely a pending dialog held by the playwright session', post-mortem 'beforeunload dialog stuck tab t2 (agent-browser "tab is not responding"): cleared via playwright-cli dialog-dismiss + session close'.
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle never intercepts Page.javascriptDialogOpening. Dialog state lives in whichever CDP client opened it, so one driver can orphan a dialog on a browser other clients depend on, and the victim gets a generic 'tab is not responding'. Nothing warns that accepting a beforeunload discards unsaved page state.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Daemon-owned dialog interception: pending dialogs (type + message) in `cuttle status` and prefixed onto any command that would otherwise hang, `cuttle dialog list|accept|dismiss` independent of the driver session that triggered it, and an explicit warning when the pending dialog is beforeunload.

ranked_issues.issue: cuttle owns no secret-injection path, so the driver's attach-time substitution types unknown names literally into live fields, cannot reach run-code at all, and three sessions independently reinvented the same native-value-setter DOM hack
ranked_issues.frequency: 8 sessions across the two failure shapes; two human credential takeovers, one wrongly-aborted task, two burned TOTP attempts
ranked_issues.evidence: S08: `fill f7e182 HC_PASS` returned 'len=7' with no warning and a 24-char control secret landed as len=11; the agent concluded 'The secret-substitution path drops characters - a driver bug' and aborted the whole task to a human handoff before finding the truth: 'HC_PASS is 7 characters, TEST_SECRET is 11 - exactly the lengths that landed. Nothing was truncated; it typed the literal variable names.' S01 hit the same on a government portal ('Campo demasiado pequeno') and the user entered the credentials themselves, with visible frustration at having to re-explain the flow. S16 established the complementary hole: 'playwright-cli's secrets substitution doesn't work inside run-code at all (no process.env in the sandbox)', so S11 inlined a live OTP into argv: `run-code "async page => { await page.keyboard.type('<otp>', { delay: 150 }); }"`. The reinvented hack appears verbatim in S23, S26, S27 and S33.
ranked_issues.root_cause: Secret substitution is a driver env-var feature evaluated once at session create, applying only to that driver's discrete fill/type verbs. Nothing errors on an unknown name, nothing verifies redaction is armed on an already-attached session, and a time-bounded secret cannot be refreshed without a new attach (S04 accumulated sessions bt, bt2, bt3 against one browser in 90 seconds).
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Daemon-owned secret injection at the CDP Input layer, resolved at use time - a named secret any driver can reference in any call shape, delivered as real keystrokes, never crossing argv or the transcript - with a hard error on an unknown name and `cuttle secret set NAME --from-command 'op item get ... --otp'` for time-bounded values.

ranked_issues.issue: Nothing observes the network or console, so agents monkey-patch window.fetch from inside the page, grep console log files by mtime, and download the site's own JS bundles to find out why an action failed - including the whole class where an HTTP 200 silently discarded the write
ranked_issues.frequency: 7 sessions; the 200-that-did-nothing case is the third mechanism the #1 cluster wrongly absorbed and no daemon-side settle verdict can ever catch it
ranked_issues.evidence: S04 rewrote the page's networking stack to spy on itself - `window.fetch=async (...a)=>{...window.__net.push(o.method+' '+u+' :: '+String(o.body))...}` plus XMLHttpRequest.open/send - then grepped the app's bundles from inside the page to recover an enum (`five_eight_years` -> `eight_or_more_years`) after three guessed values 400'd; separately its skills PATCH 'was accepted but ignored' - HTTP 200, zero change, caught only by habit. S13 had to confirm `POST /user/availability => [200]` from a request log. S09's a hosting provider Submit failure (a 403 on /api/jwt) was found only by `ls -t .playwright-cli/console-*.log | head -1 | xargs grep -iE '403'`, and every result reported '183 console errors' on a professional social network so the counter was useless as a signal. S06 could not inspect a redirect chain, substituted an in-page fetch with different cookie semantics, and committed a wrong 'stale cache' conclusion into a project journal.
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle proxies the whole CDP Network and Runtime domains and retains none of it; drivers expose an unfiltered request log and a raw console-error count that large SPAs baseline in the hundreds.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle net --tail` / `cuttle console --since-last-action` per seed: failed requests with status, redirect chains with final URL, request/response bodies for the action just performed, and only console entries new since the previous action, classified rather than counted.

ranked_issues.issue: Session state is lost silently by four independent routes that all return err == nil, and the standard driver call (browser.newContext) puts pages exactly where capture and restore cannot see them
ranked_issues.frequency: 3 sessions, all found by source review or infra work rather than by a session failing - the consequence lands in a later session as a routine re-login (blind spot 7)
ranked_issues.evidence: S03: 'storage.GetCookies() is called with no BrowserContextID, so it resolves to the default context only... a capture that returns err == nil (so the if !ok bail never fires), overwrites the prior good snapshot last-writer-wins, and then pool.go:628 deletes the profile dir. Cookies for that context are lost on every capture; its localStorage *is* captured, so the snapshot is left internally inconsistent.' S12: 'browser.newContext() creates an incognito context... Cuttle's own code says its restore path cannot reach it', plus '/data on no volume in either compose or helm' - the advertised persistent-logins feature quietly inert in production. Fourth route: idle reap discards the profile because --keep-profile defaults false.
ranked_issues.root_cause: Every loss path is invisible at the moment it happens, and cuttle has no way to tell a client that the context it just created is outside the state boundary.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Union cookies across all contexts, refuse to overwrite a good snapshot with an empty one, and warn at the point of loss - 'your login will not survive because X' - including when a client creates a context the restore path cannot reach and when a reap is about to discard a profile.

ranked_issues.issue: Daemon and Chrome death is invisible to attached clients: a panic surfaces as a bare ECONNREFUSED or a 502 whose body parses as success, a vanished page carries no attribution, and `cuttle status`'s log tail is 20 lines of dbus noise
ranked_issues.frequency: 5 sessions; two releases shipped carrying a live crash because the harness was green while the daemon it drove had died
ranked_issues.evidence: S03: 'My earlier confirmed fixed was wrong: I checked at 23:49, and the daemon panicked at 23:51:20, after the harness finished' - the panic (`chromedp.NewContext.func1() chromedp.go:199`) found only by reading pod exit state. S07 lost a filled wizard step to 'Daemon process exited with code 1 [PlaywrightError: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9222]' while `cuttle status`'s entire 20-line log window was repeats of '[ERROR:dbus/bus.cc:405] Failed to connect to the bus'. S12 spent hours and three subagents on 'Target page, context or browser has been closed' while 'Cuttle's own logs show the a link-aggregator site Chromes are not crashing - clean disconnected + state captured ~2s after connect', and separately: 'cuttle answers a dead Chrome with a 502 whose body is valid JSON, so it degrades to chrome ?, unknown persona instead of naming the failure.'
ranked_issues.root_cause: No health or liveness surface a driving agent can poll, no per-teardown attribution (client closeTarget vs transport drop vs idle reap vs crash), a status log tail biased toward benign Chromium noise, and error responses shaped identically to success.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle status` reporting daemon uptime, restart/panic count with stack, and last-capture outcomes; per-page teardown attribution surfaced in the CDP error path; error bodies that cannot be parsed as the success shape; and a log tail biased toward panic/fatal/exit lines.

ranked_issues.issue: Redaction is driver-side, all-or-nothing and destructive: it shreds unrelated output when secrets are short, blocks reading legitimate page data, and secrets still leak through snapshots, URLs in retry logs and the transcript
ranked_issues.frequency: 5 sessions; one real credential rotation, one exposed live session key, two OTPs in plaintext
ranked_issues.evidence: S26: `snapshot | grep -iE 'error|textbox'` returned `- textbox "Password..." [ref=e28]: t2J6bXyCQumuF!cukv` - the standard way to diagnose a failed login is a credential exfiltration path. S14 produced a rotation-requiring incident: with per-digit secrets loaded, output came back as `Console: <secret>MBCP_MC_<secret>MBCP_MC_5</secret></secret> errors` and even refs were redacted (`textbox "5ª" [ref=e<secret>MBCP_P5</secret>]`), so the agent detached to read the page - and that snapshot printed three of the user's seven multicanal digits in plaintext; in the same session the human's SMS OTP entered the transcript because there is no hand-in path. ranked_issues.root_cause: Redaction is a naive global substring replace over all driver output, armed once at attach - simultaneously too broad (destroys refs, timestamps, counts) and too narrow (misses snapshot input values and credential-shaped URL params).
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Daemon-side, value-scoped, always-on masking of exactly the values cuttle injected; snapshot-side redaction of password/one-time-code inputs and credential-shaped URL params; `cuttle secret prompt` so a human can hand over an OTP without it entering the transcript; and a sanctioned read-out path that writes a scraped credential to a file instead of through the model's context.

ranked_issues.issue: There is no upload path into the containerized browser: the driver's upload verb is gated on an already-armed file chooser, fails silently when it is not, and nobody documents whether a path resolves on the host or in the container
ranked_issues.frequency: 5 sessions; one permanently incomplete legal filing and one wrong-widget upload on a live account. Under-counted by construction - S07 simply never tried, and that only surfaced because the human asked
ranked_issues.evidence: S07: 'On the documents: yes, there was an upload field, and I missed it' - by the time the human asked ('and wasn't there any place in form to submit docs?') the wizard had locked the a national tax id with `attachmentsJSON: ""`, forcing the document out of band by email. S02 ran `docker cp /tmp/kc-logo.png cuttle:/tmp/...`, then `agent-browser upload` reported success while a hand-written probe returned `{files:0}`; only `page.setInputFiles` with a Mac path worked, making the docker cp dead work. S04 got `Error: The tool "browser_file_upload" can only be used when there is related modal state present`, then guessed a control and fired a PDF at the cover-image uploader on the user's live account. S01 hit the mirror error: 'Tool browser_snapshot does not handle the modal state.'
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle owns the downloads direction and not its mirror. Upload is per-driver behaviour keyed to modal state, with no way to name the target input and no documented path-resolution rule for a browser that runs in a container.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle upload <selector-or-index> <local-file>` that stages the file and sets it via CDP DOM.setFileInputFiles regardless of modal state, returning the file name and byte count as the page sees it; plus one SKILL.md line stating which side paths resolve on.

ranked_issues.issue: In-page overlays, modals, toasts and validation messages are not perceivable - there is no 'what is on screen / what is blocking this click' read, so agents dump DOM text and guess
ranked_issues.frequency: 9 sessions; worst single episode 20 tool calls on one silently-refusing button
ranked_issues.evidence: S07 burned 20 calls on a Continue button that failed silently - 'No request fires and no console error, so client-side validation is silently refusing' - and eventually fetched the site's own LWC bundle and grepped it to find 'Address * - Minimum 3 characters and maximum 35'. S21's first click died on a backdrop visible only in the timeout body: '<div class="fixed inset-0 z-50 ... backdrop-blur-sm"> intercepts pointer events'. S10 queried [role=alert] for a validation error and got the cookie-consent banner. S22's submit confirmation was a self-closing alertdialog the agent caught by luck, then had to prove the submission via a a webmail client receipt.
ranked_issues.root_cause: No cuttle-level page-state primitive. The a11y snapshot lists overlay content without indicating it covers the page, and transient UI is gone by the time a snapshot polls for it.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle look` / `cuttle overlays` reporting the top layer, the element actually under the intended click point, rendered validation text with shadow DOM flattened, plus a short rolling per-tab log of dialog/toast/navigation events so 'what appeared in the last 10s' is answerable after the fact.

ranked_issues.issue: Humanized typing is slow, capped and silently bypassed above the cap, and it outruns the driver's fixed 5s action timeout - producing hard TimeoutErrors on writes that actually succeeded, on live accounts
ranked_issues.frequency: 7 sessions on the latency/cap half, 2 on the false-timeout half; several minutes of blocking wall clock per long field
ranked_issues.evidence: S16 measured the cliff exactly: 'short (16) -> 2537ms, 159ms/char; at cap (80) -> 11996ms, 150ms/char; over cap (140) -> 8ms, 0ms/char' - confirmed in source at humanize.go:156 (`insertTextMaxRunes = 80`) and humanize.go:592, where anything longer commits through insertText unhumanized with no signal. S01's 33-row IBAN loop ran 16:19:54 -> 16:24:26 for ~950 characters and the BIC column could not be filled at all, so the agent edited the XML offline and re-uploaded - which triggered the Leave-site dialog that wiped the live draft. S10 routed a 3386-char body through `page.keyboard.insertText`, i.e. 'the fields that most need to look human were filled by the least human path'. S11 hit the false failure twice on the user's live profile: 'TimeoutError: Timeout 5000ms exceeded ... fill("Co-Founder, Baton...")' for 56 characters, where 'The fills actually landed (humanized typing just outran the CLI's 5s report window)' - a naive retry would have doubled the text.
ranked_issues.root_cause: ~130-160ms/char with an 80-rune cap and a silent fallback to one unhumanized edit, with nothing negotiating the driver's default action timeout against that pacing and nothing documenting the arithmetic.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: A blessed bulk-text path with a stated stealth tradeoff (chunked humanized runs, or an explicit per-command opt-out), a daemon warning when a fill falls back to insertText, and cuttle extending or negotiating the attached driver's action timeout when humanization is on - failing which SKILL.md must state chars x ~130ms and the rule 'on a fill timeout, read back before retrying, never re-fill'.

ranked_issues.issue: Humanization coverage is narrow and invisible, and the humanize decision is baked at `cuttle up` so it cannot be revised once the agent learns what kind of work the task is
ranked_issues.frequency: 6 sessions on the coverage half, 3 on the toggle half; `--humanize` appears in 176 commands but no session ever changed it mid-task
ranked_issues.evidence: Confirmed in source: the humanizer intercepts exactly Input.dispatchMouseEvent, Input.dispatchKeyEvent and Input.insertText (humanize.go:136-138); everything through Runtime.evaluate is invisible to it and produces isTrusted=false, while SKILL.md:199-206 claimed typing was 'rewritten into human-paced motion'. S16 measured the prefilter bug across releases: 0.11.3 `fill()` took 15-19ms with 0 keydowns, 0.11.4 took 1.1s with 10 keydowns for the identical value. S01 shows the scale of the invisible bypass: 65 of its eval calls performed the actual clicks and typing via .click()/dispatchEvent/nativeInputValueSetter, none of which the daemon ever saw. On the toggle half, S04 paid ~0.5s/click for ~50 interactions on the user's own a freelance marketplace profile - five minutes to re-add ~30 skill chips with no adversary present - because switching humanize off means --recreate, discarding a session that cost a password, two failed TOTP attempts and four attach cycles.
ranked_issues.root_cause: The humanizer sits on three CDP methods with no signal to the caller when an action routes around it, and the humanize flag is a launch-time property of the container rather than of the connection.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Report humanization coverage per action (or warn when a page mutates without dispatched Input); per-connection or per-command humanize control (`?humanize=0` on the CDP attach URL alongside the existing `?fingerprint=`); and humanize state reported in `cuttle status` and the attach briefing.

ranked_issues.issue: The driver's actionability gate never settles on animated SPA and consent UIs, and a11y refs are single-use - together these are why two sessions abandoned high-level verbs permanently and fell to coordinates
ranked_issues.frequency: 6 sessions (actionability) + 7 sessions (stale refs); S01 ran snapshot:click at exactly 1:1 (261:261) because every targeted action needed a fresh snapshot first
ranked_issues.evidence: S06 told the user proactively 'a SaaS console buttons never pass Playwright's stability check (some persistent animation), so I'm clicking via DOM dispatch'. S07 on a OneTrust banner: 'waiting for element to be visible, enabled and stable' x4. S05's Google consent flow: two ref/role clicks timed out and the entire remainder of the OAuth flow ran on raw coordinates. On refs: S04 got `Error: Ref f6e811 not found in the current page snapshot` mid-form-fill leaving `year_from=""`; S05 saw `click f12e539` -> 'element was detached from the DOM, retrying' -> 'Ref f12e493 not found', with prefixes drifting e... / f12e... / f2e... between frames; S27 found the same login form's refs were e35 in one session and f7e35 in another, so no known flow can be cached.
ranked_issues.root_cause: A stability heuristic designed for static pages applied to perpetually-animating UI, plus a per-invocation process model that re-mints refs on every snapshot, with errors that name the element rather than the reason and no distinction between 'ref stale' and 'element absent'.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: A cuttle-side click that keeps trusted input while skipping the driver's stability gate (see #3); auto-resnapshot on a stale ref or stable handles that survive a re-render; and a SKILL.md rule that refs are valid only within one chained command, with a symptom-to-driver routing hint ('two consecutive actionability timeouts on an animated SPA -> switch driver, same browser, no state lost').

ranked_issues.issue: Nothing reports which element has focus or what a field's value became, so widget-specific semantics fail invisibly and produce syntactically plausible wrong values on live systems
ranked_issues.frequency: 6 sessions; two near-miss writes of wrong data to live systems, one of them a legally-binding tax form
ranked_issues.evidence: S01: campo 61 was AT-prefilled with 9,81; the agent typed 9,81 and the field became 9.819,81 - caught only by the human's eye. Same session: a fill 'landed in the portal's global search box' and cost 52 calls. S14: `click e89` 'actually focused SMS box 5', putting the first three OTP digits in boxes 5-7 (`"<redacted-id>"`), and `fill '#dtEnd' '10/08/2026'` read back as '25/06/2026 .. 10/08/2026/08/2026' because the input is masked and appends. S04: `type f6e1208 "Rust"` produced no options while `fill` on the same ref did. S06's CodeMirror writes degraded from replace to append and produced invalid JSON two clicks from being saved as live build config, and a force-click reported `{"focused":"dark | BODY"}`.
ranked_issues.root_cause: Two distinct gaps the upstream clustering scattered: no layer reports the active element after an action (separate from which tab is foreground, #2), and no doc carries the per-widget rules that every real authenticated app needs. Each failure yields a plausible wrong value rather than an error.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Report the active element and the field's before/after value on every fill/type - the single change that converts this whole class from invisible to obvious - plus a short 'modern form widgets' section in SKILL.md covering masked, React-controlled, chip/tag, multi-box OTP and rich-text inputs.

ranked_issues.issue: There is no login handoff primitive and no rule for when to use the viewer, so agents hand-roll waiters in shell, park pages in prose, and reach for the viewer neither when they should nor only when they should
ranked_issues.frequency: 6 sessions with hand-rolled waiters + 7 sessions with a mis-set handoff bar; wall-clock stalls of ~36h, ~12min and ~10min in three separate sessions
ranked_issues.evidence: S18 stalled ~36 hours on GitHub sudo mode and wrote its own waiter: `for i in $(seq 1 90); do t=$(playwright-cli --raw eval "document.title"); if [ "$t" != "Confirm access" ]; then echo "page advanced"; exit 0; fi; sleep 4; done`. S36 wrote a site-specific `fetch('/api/retail/user/current/wallet')` probe just to answer 'is this origin still authenticated'. On the bar: S04 hit a 2FA login AND walked up to an irreversible Delete on the user's live resume without ever offering the viewer, and the human intervened out of band ('i just updated the resume on resume tab myself'); S05 never opened or mentioned the viewer in 183 calls, including at the moment it handed the task back; S10 guided the human click-by-click through a professional social network report dialogs from memory, getting labels wrong three times while the human pasted a screenshot at every step. Conversely S08 aborted to the viewer for two password fields it could have typed itself, and the user pushed back: 'read cuttle's skill and check full playwright-cli skill / you should be able to do that yourself!'
ranked_issues.root_cause: The VNC viewer is cuttle's flagship handoff feature and no verb uses it; SKILL.md markets it but sets no bar, so there is no login-state probe before the wall and no completion signal after it.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle handoff <url> --until <predicate> --timeout` that opens the page, prints the exact viewer link focused on the right tab, notifies the human and returns when the page leaves the sign-in origin; `cuttle auth status <domain>` for the before half; and explicit SKILL.md triggers (real captcha, 2FA, bank step, irreversible action on a live account - not 'typing a password').

ranked_issues.issue: Handoff is one-directional and the viewer is a shared, unrecorded, single-framebuffer room: nothing tells the agent the human acted, and with two seeds up there is no per-seed view of which browser the human is even looking at
ranked_issues.frequency: 1 session narrated it three times; unmeasurable by construction - this is the mechanism behind blind spot 1, which inflates every success rate in the corpus
ranked_issues.evidence: S01, three times: 'i entered <redacted-id> myself, and it just worked... you were overthinking stuff' (after 52 agent calls on that modal), 'i did mouse drag myself, check the value now' (after four failed slider strategies), and 'i entered creds myself' - plus 'did that [screenshot]. check the current page pls', the user explicitly instructing the agent to re-read the page after acting in the viewer. Structurally: `Xvnc :99 -geometry 1920x1080` with openbox and -AlwaysShared, every seed's Chrome mapped onto that one framebuffer and sized from fingerprint.ScreenArgs, so the human who opens 6080 gets whichever window openbox has on top, not the one the agent is driving.
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle sits between the viewer and the browser and could see human-originated input, but exposes no event, no diff and no recording; and one X display serves all seeds with no per-seed viewer URL.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: A 'page changed by viewer input at T' signal in `cuttle status` and annotated onto the next driver result; a per-seed viewer URL that raises and focuses that seed's window; and SKILL.md guidance to re-read state after asking the human to do one step.

ranked_issues.issue: 'Logins persist across down/up' is not true for the sites that matter and there is no way to ask whether a seed is still authenticated, so every session opens by re-running the risky login flow
ranked_issues.frequency: 11 sessions; a fixed 3-5 call tax per session plus the credential risk of #13 and #17 paid repeatedly
ranked_issues.evidence: All three a freelance marketplace board checks (S23 Aug 6, S27 Aug 10, S33 Aug 12) opened logged out despite the persistent profile and 3008-cookie state snapshots visible in the daemon log; the agent has internalised it - 'Logged out as expected (their sessions always expire)' - and the user's workflow docs now open with 'ASSUME LOGGED OUT', which means the friction is now paid on every future run while generating no new evidence (blind spot 5). S01 found the server-side variant: 'The one thing that actually was broken: your server session had expired. Clicking Entregar an hour ago would have bounced you to the login page and wiped the draft.' S15 attached into a browser holding a timed-out a consumer banking web app tab and a logged-out a consumer banking app that both look like live logins in a tab list.
ranked_issues.root_cause: The cookie jar persists; the server-side session does not, and the briefing promise reads stronger than reality. Nothing surfaces per-origin auth state, so the only detector is landing on a sign-in redirect.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle auth status [origin]` reporting which origins have stored cookies, when state was captured and how old it is, plus a SKILL.md line stating that persisted cookies do not mean a live server session.

ranked_issues.issue: Reading a page is expensive and awkward: snapshots run to thousands of lines, land as timestamped YAML in whatever directory the shell is in, and must be found with `ls -t` and mined with rg/sed line windows - so agents only ever see the slice they already suspected mattered
ranked_issues.frequency: 10 sessions; 592 snapshot calls in the window, most of them followed by shell mining
ranked_issues.evidence: S28 reconstructed a 27-name guest list with `f=$(ls -t .playwright-cli/page-*.yml | head -1) && rg -n -i 'sign in|approved|guest' "$f"` then `sed -n '190,352p' "$f" | rg -o 'Profile picture for ([^"]+)"'`. S30 needed seven shell calls to read one a professional social network profile: snapshot -> ls -t -> rg -> sed -> run-code scroll -> snapshot -> rg. S13 grep-and-sed'd snapshots ~12 times, once getting nothing from `sed -n '150,260p'` with no idea what part of the page it had sliced. S20 read a billing page as `document.body.innerText.split('\n').slice(18,60)`.
ranked_issues.root_cause: No scoped, token-budgeted read primitive: the a11y snapshot is all-or-nothing, is written to disk by the driver rather than returned, and cuttle owns no artifact location of its own.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle read [--selector] [--region dialog] [--text|--aria]` returning a context-sized extract inline, and a stable artifact directory outside any git working tree with absolute paths printed.

ranked_issues.issue: Content the agent cannot see is systematically mistaken for content that is not there: virtualized lists, collapsed expanders and cross-origin frames all read as empty with no signal, and no count is ever reconciled
ranked_issues.frequency: 4 sessions on virtualization/disclosure, 4 sessions touching frames (11 frame-related calls in the window) - restored from the critics; both classes dissolved entirely in clustering
ranked_issues.evidence: Virtualization: S01's BIC column 'could not be filled at all' because the virtualized table held ~8 of 33 rows in the DOM - the actual reason it fell back to offline XML surgery, which the clustering misattributed to humanize latency; S09 wrote three byte-identical 251.9K PNGs of a virtualized message list without noticing; S15 saw a 'Tools 14' badge against six extractable names and burned six calls before finding a 'Show 4 more...' expander. Frames: S08's two frameLocator attempts on the cross-origin reCAPTCHA anchor returned only the waiting line and nothing else; S05's ref prefixes drifted e... / f12e... / f2e... across frames, so refs are not merely stale but invisibly namespaced; S25 got a user-pasted page ending 'this page contains 1 cross-origin iframe(s) that could not be accessed due to browser security policies'; S16 noted screenshots were 'the only tool for cross-origin iframe captchas'.
ranked_issues.root_cause: Every read primitive returns a window over the data and none of them says so. Snapshots do not span frames, there is no frame enumeration, and nothing reconciles a page's own stated count against what was extracted.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle frames` enumerating frames with origin and reachability, extraction that spans frames or names the frame it stopped at, a scroll-and-collect read that reports 'collected N of M claimed', and a stated rule that an empty result on a list-like region means 'not in DOM', not 'not on page'.

ranked_issues.issue: Every input primitive except click and type is missing, including the ones anti-bot UIs specifically gate on: no drag verb, no dwell, and hover/wheel are undocumented despite being load-bearing
ranked_issues.frequency: 3 sessions with hard blocks; only 14 hover and 3 drag commands in the entire 14-day window against 2749 driver calls - restored from the critics, who noted every input cluster was about clicking
ranked_issues.evidence: S15 polled GitHub's Authorize button five times reading `disabled=true`, and only `hover f5e83; mousewheel 0 100; sleep 4` flipped it to false - an interaction-gated control that withholds enablement until it sees human-shaped hover and scroll, which is squarely cuttle's stated territory and appears in no cluster. S01's range slider desynced three ways ('says -25, UI says 0, hidden 0') across four strategies and the human dragged it by hand. S02: 'Click landed off-screen (y=1035 vs 959 viewport)... the coordinate click silently does nothing - calendar closes, value unchanged, no error.'
ranked_issues.root_cause: The humanizer's rich behavioural modelling (curved Fitts-law motion, log-normal keystrokes) is reachable only through click and type. Drag, hover, wheel and dwell have no verb and no doc line, so the interactions most likely to be watched by an anti-bot system are the ones agents perform least naturally, or not at all.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle drag <from> <to>`, `cuttle hover <sel> [--dwell ms]` and `cuttle scroll` on the same humanized path as click, with auto-scroll-into-view before any coordinate action; plus a SKILL.md note that some controls enable only after human-shaped hover/scroll.

ranked_issues.issue: Unsaved in-page state is destroyed by at least seven independent routes with no marker and no checkpoint - the corpus's most expensive consequence class, dissolved across five clusters
ranked_issues.frequency: At least 7 distinct destruction routes across 5 sessions - restored from the critics as a cross-cutting class rather than a symptom of each mechanism
ranked_issues.evidence: The routes, each evidenced separately: beforeunload accepted (S01, tax declaration draft rebuilt twice); navigation fired while a dialog was pending (same session, SS Direta wizard lost); forced re-auth after silent server-side session expiry (S01: 'Clicking Entregar an hour ago would have bounced you to the login page and wiped the draft'); a side-lookup performed on the same tab; a concurrent client closing the tab (S05's filled Notion dialog); a browser restart the agent could not attribute (S06: 'your logged-in tabs were dropped when the browser restarted mid-session, not by me'); and a driver session teardown. No cluster proposed the one cross-cutting mitigation.
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle knows when a tab holds unsaved client-side state (it sees the beforeunload handler register) and never says so, and no layer offers a way to checkpoint a partially-filled form before a risky action.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Mark tabs holding unsaved state in `cuttle status` and in the warning on any command that would navigate, restart or accept a beforeunload; plus a `cuttle checkpoint` that snapshots form values so a destroyed draft is recoverable rather than re-entered by hand.

ranked_issues.issue: Wrong conclusions about cuttle are written durably into user repos and read back as fact by later sessions - misdiagnosis has a write path
ranked_issues.frequency: At least 3 documented instances plus three repos now carrying hand-rolled cuttle playbooks - restored from the critics, who noted the docs cluster treated repo-written playbooks purely as evidence of a vacuum, never as a contamination mechanism
ranked_issues.evidence: S02 wrote 'cuttle's Chromium never fires the lazy RSC requests' into the user's playbook and had to retract it: 'That was the whole bug - a background tab, not a cuttle limitation. Let me correct the playbook immediately.' S06 committed a 'stale cache' diagnosis into a marketing journal when the evidence showed a server-side redirect, having been unable to inspect the redirect chain (#14). The mechanism that makes this systematic is #7 (no durable home for cuttle knowledge) combined with the daemon actively falsifying diagnostics - Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled makes hasFocus() return true regardless of real input routing, so S06 published a root cause its own evidence contradicted after cycling five theories over ~10 calls.
ranked_issues.root_cause: Agents cannot introspect cuttle truthfully, so their beliefs about it are wrong at a demonstrable rate; and because cuttle offers no durable place for per-site or per-tool knowledge, those beliefs land in the user's repo where the next session reads them as ground truth.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: A truthful `cuttle status --focus` / `whoami-tab` reporting which target actually receives Input and stating that under cuttle hasFocus() and visibilityState do not predict input delivery; plus a cuttle-owned place for per-site recipes so playbooks stop being written into unrelated repos.

ranked_issues.issue: Proxy and egress - half of cuttle's stated purpose - is entirely unobservable: a plain connectOverCDP attach dies on the seed's proxy 407 with an error naming neither proxy nor remedy, and no verb reports exit IP or proxy health
ranked_issues.frequency: 3 sessions, one of which lost an entire probe run; restored from the critics - the proxy/geoip category produced zero clusters despite being a core product feature
ranked_issues.evidence: S12's subagent lost all six navigations of a probe run to `net::ERR_INVALID_AUTH_CREDENTIAL` because a plain connectOverCDP attach does not handle the seed's proxy 407: 'The probe hit the documented proxy-auth gotcha (no route handler)'. S03 saw `a link-aggregator site:search` take 55s against a usual 8-9s and wrote 'it could equally be a burned proxy exit', then dropped the question inside a release gate it was about to sign off. And the __default__ seed leak (#37) is an egress failure before it is a memory one: the raw text is 'a real headed Chrome with direct, unproxied egress'.
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle handles proxy-407 transparently over its own CDP path, but an attaching driver that does not install a route handler never benefits, and the resulting Chromium error string mentions neither proxy nor cuttle. Nothing anywhere reports the seed's exit IP, its 407 state, or whether an exit is burned.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Exit IP, proxy health and 407 state per seed in `cuttle status`; translation of ERR_INVALID_AUTH_CREDENTIAL into a cuttle error naming proxy auth and the remedy; and a briefing line telling an attaching driver what it must do to inherit proxy auth.

ranked_issues.issue: cuttle ships measurable internal fingerprint incoherences with no self-check, so agents hand-roll stealth probes that themselves lie and publish wrong verdicts
ranked_issues.frequency: 3 sessions; ~75% of production renders geometrically incoherent by one measurement - restored from the critics, who noted the clustering kept only the geometry symptom and treated persona as a reporting problem
ranked_issues.evidence: S03 published a wrong stealth verdict before catching itself: `document.fonts.check()` is unpatched and returns true for everything (clark patch catalog row 30, never implemented), so the naive probe passes on any input; the agent rebuilt the test as width-measurement against a `NotARealFont12345` control. Same session: `devicePixelRatio: 2` with `(resolution: 2dppx) = false`; `availTop: 0` with 95px removed from the bottom - a Windows taskbar layout under a macOS UA (glim-sh/cuttle#45). S12 measured the geometry end to end: 'innerWidth (1920, hardcoded by cloakbrowser's DEFAULT_VIEWPORT and again by scrapling) exceeds both outerWidth and screen.width on every render... macOS is incoherent on 5/5 of cuttle's screen pool, Windows on 3/4 - so prod is quietly incoherent ~75% of the time too.' S03 measured the attach-side mirror: 'outer=2560x1392 inner=780x403', and found http.go:196 prefixes every unknown query param as `--fingerprint-<key>=` so `--window-size` can never be passed. Sharpest instance of #7: the correct font-probing method had been discovered in a July session and existed only in a transcript.
ranked_issues.root_cause: Three different numbers (spoofed screen, OS window, driver viewport) are set by three layers that cannot see each other, several patches in the catalog are unimplemented, and cuttle neither clamps, warns, nor self-checks - so the only instrument is an agent-written probe that shares the same blind spots.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: A `cuttle verify` self-check asserting internal coherence (fonts.check against a control, dPR vs dppx, availTop/availHeight vs persona, screen vs window vs viewport) with a named pass/fail per row; detect and clamp or loudly warn when a client's viewport override contradicts the seed's spoofed screen; and report window/viewport/framebuffer geometry in `cuttle status`.

ranked_issues.issue: Second-channel legs - email and SMS confirmation codes - are a routine part of every authenticated flow in this corpus and have no path, so codes enter the transcript or the flow silently blocks
ranked_issues.frequency: 4 sessions; restored from the critics - no cluster covered the second channel itself
ranked_issues.evidence: S11 scraped a a webmail client OTP by `rg`-ing a driver-written snapshot YAML off disk, then typed it with `keyboard.type`. S14 put an SMS code in the transcript because there is no hand-in path (see #17). S08 kept clicking through a wizard while an email confirmation blocked it, until the human said 'you had to confirm the email, i just did that'. S22 could only prove a submission via a a webmail client receipt after the alertdialog self-closed.
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle treats the browser as the whole world, but every real login and most real submissions have an out-of-band leg. There is no way to wait on it, no way to hand a code in without it entering the transcript, and no way to notice that a flow is blocked on one.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle secret prompt NAME` for a human to hand in a code out of transcript (shared with #17), a documented recipe for the mail-check leg, and detection of 'this flow is waiting on an out-of-band confirmation' so it becomes a handoff trigger (#24) rather than a silent stall.

ranked_issues.issue: cuttle has no machine-readable self-description and no instance identity, so a green port probe proves nothing about which cuttle - or whether it is cuttle at all - the driver is talking to, and there is no readiness gate
ranked_issues.frequency: 4-6 infra sessions; ~60 calls and ~10 minutes of cold-start sleeping in one session alone (S03: 413 Bash calls, zero `cuttle up`/`down`/`open`, 27 cold-start sleeps totalling 602s)
ranked_issues.evidence: S12: 'A local cuttle container still on 24022 makes the port-forward's until loop spin unable to bind while the probe goes green off the local container - so --remote-browser silently runs against the local arm64/macOS farm believing it's on cluster amd64/Windows'; the fix was asserting on the persona string in the returned UA. It also had to diff local vs prod by hand: arm64/macOS vs amd64/Windows, /dev/shm 3GB vs 2Gi, --idle-timeout 90 vs 600. S32 had `ab` aliased to `agent-browser --cdp 9333` while cuttle served 9222 - any habitual use would silently drive a different browser with no error. S16's `cuttle up --image ...:0.11.3` printed the CLI's version 0.11.4 on the ready line during an A/B whose entire point was which daemon build was running. S44 wrote `docker compose up -d ... && sleep 12 && curl /json/version` by hand, then diagnosed itself: 'docker compose up -d returns when containers are created, not when they're serving', and the human's correction was blunt: 'it feels like you keep falling back to docker compose directly in most occasions' - the cost being a skipped `cuttle-smoke`.
ranked_issues.root_cause: Port reachability is treated as identity, nothing stamps which instance and seed a driver session is on, `cuttle status` reports neither the daemon's own version nor its effective configuration, and no verb blocks until the first Chrome is attachable or exits non-zero until it is.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle up --wait` and `cuttle status --json` with a ready boolean, non-zero exit until ready, daemon version, instance id, arch, persona, start time, effective flags (humanize, idle-timeout, shm), per-seed window/viewport, CDP address and bind scope - one command two instances can be diffed with and any consumer can assert against.

ranked_issues.issue: cuttle's CDP surface is unauthenticated with no bind restriction and was reachable by unauthenticated callers on the deployment network
ranked_issues.frequency: 1 session, but the exposure had been live indefinitely and was found only because an unrelated SSRF audit went looking
ranked_issues.evidence: S44, verified in a deployed environment: `glim_web_fetch("http://<deployment-host>:9222/json/version")` -> 200, returning the cuttle webSocketDebuggerUrl. The agent's commit note: 'CDP's HTTP endpoints (/json/new, /json/list) manipulate the browser farm.'
ranked_issues.root_cause: No token, no allowlist, no bind-scope default, and no way for an operator to see which interface the CDP port is bound to.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: A shared-secret/bearer token on the CDP HTTP+WS surface, loopback-only binding by default with an explicit opt-in to listen wider, and bind scope reported in `cuttle status`.

ranked_issues.issue: A plain discovery GET to /json/version launches the reserved __default__ seed - a real headed Chrome with direct unproxied egress - which is never reaped because no CDP connection arms the idle reaper
ranked_issues.frequency: 1 session, but it is a permanent resource and egress leak per probing consumer, and it was landing on the canary that had just been tuned to mirror prod memory exactly
ranked_issues.evidence: S12, review finding then confirmed live: 'describeFarm() sends no ?fingerprint=, so cuttle launches the reserved __default__ seed - a real headed Chrome with direct, unproxied egress - and because a discovery-only GET never opens a CDP connection, the idle reaper is never armed, so it is never reaped. Confirmed live: /data/__default__ is running in the local container right now.'
ranked_issues.root_cause: Metadata discovery and browser provisioning share an endpoint, and reaper arming is tied to CDP connect rather than to spawn.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Serve /json/version metadata without spawning a seed (or arm the reaper on spawn, or refuse __default__ for discovery), plus a cheap describe-farm endpoint that costs no browser - and note the egress half belongs with #32, not with memory accounting.

ranked_issues.issue: Driver ergonomics have no contract: output is double-JSON-encoded and mixed with progress chatter, inline JS cannot survive shell quoting, scratch artifacts land in the user's git tree, and verb discovery happens by trial and error mid-task
ranked_issues.frequency: 11 sessions on verb discovery, 9 on quoting (~30 throwaway .js files), 8 on output parsing, 6 on scratch placement - individually small, collectively a multiplier on every session
ranked_issues.evidence: Output: S29 hit `jq: error (at board.json:1): Cannot index string with string ("data")` on a raw body of `"{\"data\":[{\"mid\":..."`, re-applied the `jq -r .` fix to four separate fetches, then wrote it into CLAUDE.md as gotcha #1 noting 'Nothing in CLAUDE.md warns about it'; S07 lost two calls to JSONDecodeError because even --raw output carries ANSI-dim '- fonts loaded' lines and an appended 'Shell cwd was reset'. Quoting: S06 wrote 21 of its 40 run-code calls to a file because nested quoting could not survive `page.locator('button:has(use[href=\"...\"])')`; S22's heredoc failed with a misleading `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')'`. Scratch: S02 swept ~3,100 lines of console logs and page snapshots into a git commit; S18 was hard-blocked by a stale zero-byte `.playwright-cli` file (`Error: EEXIST ... mkdir '~/Projects/pond/.playwright-cli'`) after the failing command had already opened a tab; S05 prefixed all 183 calls with `cd <scratchpad> &&`. Discovery: three different wrong tab verbs in three sessions (`new-tab` S23, `tabs` S26, `navigate` S27), each answered with a 40-line usage block and no 'did you mean'; S04 interleaved `playwright-cli --help | grep -iE "^  (goto|open|nav|tab)"` with real work on a live account. Also here: per-invocation process startup dominates discrete loops (S16 measured attach 498ms, tab-list 235ms, 10 Hacker News rows in 33ms batched vs ~797ms per discrete round trip), and the two obvious efficiency moves are mutually incompatible because batched refs die on mutations the earlier steps caused (S21).
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle delegates the entire agent-facing surface to third-party CLIs and documents none of their contracts: no stated output shape per verb, no artifact location of its own, no inlined verb cheat sheet, and no statement that run-code is not atomic.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: A thin `cuttle exec` / `cuttle eval --file --json` emitting only payload on stdout and diagnostics on stderr; a cuttle-owned per-session artifact directory outside any git tree with absolute paths printed; and a `cuttle up` briefing that inlines the 6-8 verbs every session needs per driver plus the batching rule and its counter-rule.

ranked_issues.issue: Lifecycle and compatibility changes are silent: `cuttle up` restarts and discards the tab set with no reason, --recreate's effect on the profile is ambiguous, a bare navigation timeout carries no forensics, removed entrypoints and env vars fail with no message, and CUTTLE_PORT collides with Kubernetes service-link injection
ranked_issues.frequency: 3 sessions on lifecycle, 3 on timeout forensics, 1 each on the shim and the k8s collision - plus a ~4-minute production outage
ranked_issues.evidence: Lifecycle: S40's `cuttle up` returned 'cuttle restarted' and the browser came back with only about:blank - the same command printed 'already running' in two other sessions - with no reason and no warning that the human's logged-in tabs were gone; S07's agent fell back to `docker volume ls` and `docker inspect` because 'the status text from the older image says it discards the profile'; S06 could not attribute tab loss at all. Also here, a benign-but-corrosive one: `playwright-cli attach` routinely prints session-created and `Error: Target page, context or browser has been closed` together (S06's first browser call, and S25 identically), apparently binding to cuttle's immortal keep-alive about:blank, costing ~8 calls of defensive re-attaching. Forensics: S44's 'Two 25s attempts -> browser tier timed out x2 -> 51s -> outcome: timeout' with Loki showing a cloud document suite at 5 attempts / 0 successes over 30 days, one of which was a user whose third try was `/export?format=txt` - 'which also failed... because a browser navigating to a text/plain download produces nothing'; S03 reported then retracted an improvement because a short-video platform flipped pass/fail across runs; S12's subagent: 'A genuine silent challenge would look identical.' Compatibility: S03 found '/usr/local/bin/cuttleserve shim is gone... CLOAKBROWSER_BINARY_PATH is no longer read' with three call sites that would not start; S12 found 'naming the Service cuttle makes k8s inject CUTTLE_PORT=tcp://<cluster-ip>:9222, which collides with cuttle's own --port config var' - CrashLoopBackOff, browser farm down, and 'helmfile template could never catch this; it's a runtime injection'.
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle reports outcomes without causes across its whole operator surface: restarts without reasons, timeouts without evidence, removed contracts without diagnostics, and a config namespace (CUTTLE_*) that is exactly the namespace Kubernetes reserves for service links.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: State the restart reason and warn that the tab set was discarded; make --recreate print which profile volume it re-attaches; attach cheap forensics to any navigation timeout (last committed URL, title, bytes extracted, content-type, challenge-sentinel match) with a caller-settable per-attempt budget; a one-release deprecation shim that starts and names the change; reject a CUTTLE_PORT that looks like `tcp://host:port` and say so at startup; and hide or mark the keep-alive target so drivers stop reporting a benign error on attach.

ranked_issues.issue: The container boundary and the local-vs-production divergence are undocumented, so the workflow cuttle should most obviously own - verify my local UI change in a real browser - silently routes around it
ranked_issues.frequency: 4 sessions on the host boundary, 3 on arch divergence; one session drove a browser 27 times against http://localhost:5173 and never touched cuttle at all
ranked_issues.evidence: S02 first opened `http://host.docker.internal:4321/`, flip-flopped to the LAN address `http://<lan-ip>:4321/`, then killed the user's dev server and restarted it with `pnpm dev --host` purely so the containerized browser could reach it, hardcoding a machine-specific IP into a dozen subsequent calls. S19 drove a browser 27 times against localhost:5173 with cuttle untouched. On divergence, S03: a large e-commerce site 'exceeds page.goto's 45s timeout before it ever gets to the anti-bot check', a short-video platform/a large social network 'blow the web tier's 25s render budget' under qemu - and the human, not the agent, unblocked it ('can you do run on ssh <remote-host> for example then to check?'), with native measurement showing 'identity:us took 2.5s on <remote-host> vs 9.2s locally'; the gate meant to catch this was itself misconfigured ('the canary was provisioned at half of prod's memory, and a disk-backed emptyDir for /dev/shm where prod has a tmpfs'), and S12 later found a 'canary-only, blame qemu' comment had been covering a permanent a large social network failure on production-identical amd64 for months.
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle runs the browser in Docker on a multi-arch image where the arch selects the stealth persona and the render budget is a fixed constant, and says nothing about the network boundary, the filesystem boundary, or the fact that a local failure is indistinguishable from a real one.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: A documented stable in-container hostname for the host (or `cuttle open --host-port 4321` setting up the forward) plus a line stating host paths are not visible to the browser; a loud startup warning when running translated ('render budgets are not meaningful here'); the native-arm64 image named as the local-dev path; and a per-invocation render budget.

ranked_issues.issue: Irreversible outward actions from a logged-in account have no per-action gate, and anti-bot challenge type cannot be identified so agents fight the wrong challenge
ranked_issues.frequency: 3 sessions on destructive actions (producing the corpus's sharpest user reaction), 1 on challenge detection
ranked_issues.evidence: S04 clicked Delete and then 'Yes, delete' on the user's live resume with only a local backup as mitigation; the user's next message was 'i just updated the resume on resume tab myself'. S12 produced the corpus's sharpest reaction - 'stop stop stop! no issue creation anywhere! what are you doing! i never allowed that!' - while another session's user said 'submit all of them' about equivalent form submits, so the tolerance varies sharply and cannot be inferred. On challenges, S08 ran `mousemove 1392 636; mousedown; mouseup; sleep 8` returning `{"tokenLen":0,"challengeVisible":false}`, plus a 12-iteration polling loop and a `sleep 25`, before concluding 'That's the invisible reCAPTCHA badge, not a checkbox - it mints the token on submit. So nothing to click.'
ranked_issues.root_cause: Plan-level agreement is treated as authorization for each outward act, and nothing marks destructive affordances on a live account as requiring fresh confirmation. Separately, no verb or recipe reports which challenge is present or whether it needs interaction, and cross-origin frame timeouts (#28) say nothing useful.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: SKILL.md names destructive affordances on live accounts as a handoff trigger (park the page, print the viewer URL, ask), any cuttle verb performing an irreversible outward action requires per-action confirmation, and `cuttle challenge detect` (or a documented recipe) reports challenge type and whether interaction is required - paired with the scaled element capture from #10 so an image captcha is legible in one call.

ranked_issues.issue: cuttle is not reached for when it should be: agents answer from stale cached fetches on pages the user has a live login for, and the human has to say the word 'cuttle' before a browser is considered
ranked_issues.frequency: 5 sessions; one confidently-wrong research answer and one feature shipped without ever being verified against the real dashboard
ranked_issues.evidence: S30 researched a logged-in-only a professional social network profile from a stale cached public snapshot and reported it as current; the user pushed twice - 'Are you sure that you checked the correct profile?' then 'check hher profile with cuttle' - before the agent ran `which cuttle`. S25's 'try getting those notion pages content through cuttle' was sent only after glim_web_fetch timed out on both URLs. S32 needed three discovery calls after the human said 'could you also use cuttle'. A separate session hit a hard login wall ('Privy needs an emailed code'), abandoned the real dashboard, verified against a throwaway stub route, shipped, and told the user 'One thing left for you, since I can't log in' - having never loaded cuttle at all.
ranked_issues.root_cause: Skill triggering keys on the word 'browser' rather than on the intents that actually need cuttle: read this page behind a login; a fetch returned a JS shell, a login wall, or a timeout.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Trigger the skill on read/open-this-page intents, state the escalation rule explicitly in the briefing (any fetch returning a JS shell, a login wall or a timeout is a cuttle job), and have `cuttle status` list which origins the profile currently holds sessions for so the answer to 'do I have a login for this' costs one call.
