ranked_issues.issue: Recurring authenticated jobs have no durable home, so per-site knowledge is re-derived every run and users end up demanding hand-written recipes in their own repos
ranked_issues.frequency: 6 sessions; measured payoff of codification is 24 calls / 11.6 min -> 2 calls / 47s for the same job
ranked_issues.evidence: S29's user: 'why each time it takes so much time for you to just fetch data and compare it with ... could you update pjs/career/CLAUDE.md so that when i ask you to check for new missions on a freelance marketplace - it would be the straightforward workflow for you without erroring on each step?' - and the agent's five listed causes were four browser/driver frictions. S16 quantified it: 'codifying the a freelance marketplace check into 4 commands + a baseline TSV took a recurring job from 24 calls / 11.6 min to 2 calls / 47s.' Two other sessions wrote a consumer banking web app and a professional social network recipes only after paying full price. This is the same vacuum as #7 and the write path in #31, but the cost here is recurring rather than one-off, in a corpus dominated by recurring authenticated checks.
ranked_issues.root_cause: cuttle has a `context` concept but nothing carries a per-site playbook alongside a seed, so the discovery cost of every authenticated dashboard is paid on every visit by every session.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Per-seed/per-site recipes attached to a cuttle context - at minimum a documented convention and location - so a working sequence becomes a durable asset instead of a one-off discovery, and so recipes stop landing in unrelated user repos where they contaminate later sessions.

ranked_issues.issue: Getting a file out of the browser is one-directional and brittle: `cuttle downloads` needs an exact filename with no --latest or glob, and a resource the site renders inline has no capture path
ranked_issues.frequency: 3 sessions; ~50 calls in the one session that leaned on downloads as its verification channel
ranked_issues.evidence: S01 tracked Chrome's dedup counter by hand across the session - `(3).xml` through `(9).xml` - listing the download directory whenever it lost count; when a PDF opened in a viewer tab instead of downloading, `cuttle downloads` reported nothing and the agent wrote `page.evaluate('async () => { const r = await fetch(...); const b = await r.blob(); const a = document.createElement(...)')` to synthesize a download it could then retrieve. S02 needed three navigations to surface a full-res image URL it could then fetch.
ranked_issues.root_cause: The downloads surface serves only files Chrome happened to write, addressed by exact name; authenticated resources rendered in-page have no capture path.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle downloads --latest` with glob support, and `cuttle grab <url> [dest]` performing an in-profile authenticated fetch that writes bytes host-side (the natural sibling of #9's `cuttle fetch`).

ranked_issues.issue: `Target.createBrowserContext` is blocked with a message that names no escape hatch, truncates before its remedy, and addresses an audience that cannot act on it
ranked_issues.frequency: 3 sessions; ~15 diagnosis calls plus a full release cycle (implement, review, 319-test gate, image build, canary) and one production browser tier down
ranked_issues.evidence: S03: the failure reached the client as a truncated `502 ... {"error": "Browser.new_context: Protocol error (Target.createBrowserContext): Target.createBrowserContext is blocked by cuttle: one identity per seed - attach to the existing default context, or start` - cut off mid-sentence, six times. 'There is no opt-out flag or env var - I grepped for one.' The remedy is addressed to whoever wrote the CDP call, but 'scrapling inside scraping-py calls Browser.new_context internally. That is third-party code we don't control.' The user redirected the whole task: 'lets instead of changing anything on the side of this project - go and make ~/pj/cuttle/ fully compatible first'. S16 hit the same wall later and had to `cuttle up --help | rg -i allow-context` to find the flag.
ranked_issues.root_cause: A protocol-level block shipped without a documented opt-out, with a remedy sentence aimed at the wrong audience and long enough to be truncated by every error-wrapping layer above it. Note the block also interacts with #15: newContext is exactly where state capture cannot reach.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Lead the rejection with the actionable token in the first 80 characters ('set --allow-context-creation / CUTTLE_ALLOW_CONTEXT_CREATION=1 if your driver cannot attach'), and a compatibility section in SKILL.md listing which stacks call newContext internally.

ranked_issues.issue: The humanizer's own pre-click probes ran in the main world at up to ~17 evaluates per click - the anti-detection feature was itself detectable
ranked_issues.frequency: 1 session found it; fixed in 0.11.4 (verified in source: Page.createIsolatedWorld at humanize.go:1036). Ranked low only because it is fixed - its historical cost is unmeasurable and lands in blind spot 3
ranked_issues.evidence: S16: humanize.go:693 sent Runtime.evaluate with no contextId. Measured on live containers: 0.11.3 leaked 2 observable main-world probes per click, 0.11.4 leaks 0. The upstream project had already shipped a release for the same class: 'Fix humanize=True triggering invisible CAPTCHA challenges during clicks. Humanized pre-click checks are now stealth-safe.' For the entire life of 0.11.3 the cost would have landed in transcripts as 'a captcha appeared and the agent fought it', filed against the site.
ranked_issues.root_cause: Pre-click state probes were issued into the page's own JS context, observable to any page watching for injected evaluation.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Fixed. The durable gap is the regression guard: a test asserting zero main-world evaluates per humanized action, and a standing rule that any daemon-side probing of the page uses an isolated world by construction.

ranked_issues.issue: Two operator-facing footguns with no guard: WebAuthn/passkey support is undocumented so the auth method most accounts are moving to gets routed around, and nothing prevents a second cuttle landing on the same host or names the per-seed memory cost
ranked_issues.frequency: 1 session each; one ~36h stall and one historical node OOM
ranked_issues.evidence: S18: 'I picked GitHub Mobile over the passkey (the container browser reports only partial passkey support) and over the authenticator app (that would mean you reading a TOTP code into the transcript)' - the resulting handoff stalled the whole workstream ~36 hours, and both rejected options are cuttle gaps (#13/#17 for the TOTP half). S44 had to encode a do-not-do-this into a handoff plan: never rename the helm release because 'helmfile won't uninstall a vanished release and you'd end up with a second 6Gi farm on the ~6.9Gi browser node (the 2026-06-12 OOM)'. A separate local investigation measured the cuttle container at 26-32% of a host core - roughly two-thirds of all OrbStack CPU - during unrelated work.
ranked_issues.root_cause: WebAuthn status in cuttle's Chromium is undocumented so agents probe it and route around it; per-seed memory cost is undocumented and nothing detects a second cuttle already holding the profile dir or port.
ranked_issues.capability_gap: Document WebAuthn status explicitly in SKILL.md and consider a virtual-authenticator or host-passkey bridge for the handoff path; document per-seed memory cost in the briefing and have the daemon refuse or loudly warn when another cuttle already holds the profile dir or port.

clustered_issues.issue: Agents have no visual ground truth: cuttle ships no screenshot verb and nothing in the briefing or SKILL.md tells an agent to look at the page, so most sessions took zero screenshots and substituted DOM/JSON reads that lied.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S01: verb breakdown of 628 driver calls was snapshot 245, eval 208, click 69, screenshot 6; the user finally had to ask 'are you able to screenshot the whole page so that you won't be guessing so much missing stuff from what is actually on screen?' and later caught a wrong tax figure himself ('and check the screenshot, you did some shit' - campo 61 read 9.819,81). S05: zero screenshots in 183 browser calls, 27 evals whose only job was getBoundingClientRect, 21 raw mousemove/mousedown/mouseup triplets, and 13 consecutive clicks landing on the human's tab before she hit interrupt. S17: zero screenshots in 29 calls while the human pasted [Image #1]-[Image #12]; S04 shipped a profile with eight empty image slots until the user sent a screenshot ('you forgot to add imags for each project').
clustered_issues.root_cause: cuttle has no screenshot/peek verb of its own; visual capture is entirely inherited driver behaviour that no cuttle doc mentions, and SKILL.md gives no rule for when looking beats another selector probe. The one driver whose SKILL.md agents read says screenshots are 'rarely used, as snapshot is more common'.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle shot [--tab N] [--full] [--element sel] -o file` capturing straight off CDP/the existing framebuffer, plus a SKILL.md rule naming the four situations where an image is the cheapest answer (two consecutive no-op actions, an icon-only control, a control that reports enabled but does nothing, any visual-judgment request).
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: Pervasive. Conservatively 150+ calls corpus-wide on multi-turn misdiagnoses that one image would have ended, plus every human screenshot round-trip.

clustered_issues.issue: When agents do reach for the driver's screenshot it is unreliable and awkward: 5s font-loading timeouts, silent failures that write no file, the wrong flag name, unknown output paths, and no full-page/scaled/element capture.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S04: three identical hard failures - 'TimeoutError: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. Call log: - taking page screenshot - waiting for fonts to load... - fonts loaded' at 18:37:30, 19:00:31 and 19:01:09 on three unrelated sites - after which the agent abandoned visual verification entirely. S22: `screenshot --filename=$D/billing.png >/dev/null 2>&1; echo ok` printed 'ok' and the next Read returned 'File does not exist.' S09: `--path=` was rejected with a help dump (the flag is `--filename`), and three captures of a virtualized list produced three byte-identical 251.9K PNGs. S08 needed `--hires` plus a hand-written PIL 5x upscale to read a 140x60 captcha.
clustered_issues.root_cause: Playwright's page-screenshot path waits on document.fonts.ready, which does not settle in cuttle's container - almost certainly the metric-renamed win/mac font packs the image installs. Everything else (path vs filename, cwd-relative output, no scale/clip) is un-owned driver surface.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: A daemon-side capture (CDP Page.captureScreenshot with clip + deviceScaleFactor, no font gate) that echoes an absolute output path and a content hash; and a fix or documented warning for the font-ready hang in the image.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~40 calls plus one shipped visual defect (S04) and several abandoned visual-verification strategies.

clustered_issues.issue: Native JS dialogs (beforeunload/alert/confirm) are invisible to the agent: commands silently stall behind a pending dialog, and accepting one destroys unsaved client-side state with no warning.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S01: four separate 'Leave site?' episodes on a completed tax declaration; agent narration 'The draft is still alive - the navigation is stuck on the pending dialog' followed later by 'The navigation had already fired, so the in-browser draft is gone'; user: 'can you do those changes without reuploading the file now? i'm tired of you getting stuck on Leave site? screens'. Only 4 dialog-accept and 1 dialog-dismiss calls exist in the whole 892-call session - every other dialog was discovered by inference after commands stopped working. S02 recorded the same shape in its post-mortem.
clustered_issues.root_cause: cuttle never intercepts Page.javascriptDialogOpening. Dialog state is per-driver-session and invisible to `cuttle status`, and nothing warns that accepting a beforeunload discards unsaved page state.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Daemon-owned dialog awareness: surface pending dialogs (type + message) in `cuttle status` and as a prefix on any command that would otherwise hang, with a default policy and an explicit warning when the pending dialog is beforeunload.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~30 calls plus one destroyed tax declaration draft (rebuilt twice) and one lost SS Direta wizard.

clustered_issues.issue: A JS dialog held open by one attached driver wedges the tab for every other client, and the second driver's error names the wrong cause - a failure only the multiplexer can prevent.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S02, switching drivers mid-task: 't2 is stuck - likely a pending dialog held by the playwright session. Clearing it from that side first.' Post-mortem: 'beforeunload dialog stuck tab t2 (agent-browser "tab is not responding"): cleared via playwright-cli dialog-dismiss + session close (detach only - browser survived)'.
clustered_issues.root_cause: Dialog ownership lives in whichever CDP client opened it. cuttle multiplexes CDP but does not own dialog state, so one driver can orphan a dialog on a browser other clients depend on; the victim gets a generic 'tab is not responding'.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: cuttle intercepts javascriptDialogOpening itself and exposes `cuttle dialog accept|dismiss|list` independent of the driver session that triggered it.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~10 calls plus a mid-task driver switch.

clustered_issues.issue: In-page overlays, modals, toasts and validation messages are not perceivable - there is no 'what is on screen / what is blocking this click' read, so agents dump DOM text and guess.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S07: 20 tool calls on a Continue button that failed silently - 'No request fires and no console error, so client-side validation is silently refusing' -> the agent eventually fetched the site's own LWC bundle and grepped it to find 'Address * - Minimum 3 characters and maximum 35'. S21: the first click died on a backdrop only visible in the timeout body - '<div class="fixed inset-0 z-50 ... backdrop-blur-sm"> intercepts pointer events'. S10: querying [role=alert] for a validation error returned the cookie-consent banner instead. S22: the submit confirmation was a self-closing alertdialog the agent caught by luck, then had to prove the submission via a a webmail client receipt.
clustered_issues.root_cause: No cuttle-level page-state primitive. The accessibility snapshot lists overlay content without indicating it covers the page, and transient UI (toasts, auto-dismissing dialogs) is gone by the time a snapshot polls for it.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: A `cuttle overlays` / `cuttle look` verb reporting the top layer, any element under the intended click point, rendered validation text (shadow DOM flattened), and a short rolling log of dialog/toast/navigation events per tab so 'what appeared in the last 10s' is answerable after the fact.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~70 calls across the batch; the single worst episode was 20.

clustered_issues.issue: Input dispatched to a non-foreground tab is silently swallowed and background tabs get zero rAF, so actionability never settles and lazy loaders never fire - one root cause that wore four different disguises for two weeks.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S16 measured it: 'noDefaults:true G/background -> fps 0, click FAIL 15002ms (waiting for element to be visible, enabled and stable)' vs 'noDefaults:false G/background -> fps 61, click OK 851ms'; corpus stat 139 timeout-signature results (4.9% of 2827 browser calls), '0/8 identical retries ever worked'. S05: 'The tab is backgrounded (visibilityState: hidden), so Google's UI won't respond' - rediscovered at least four separate times. S02 spent 58 calls concluding 'cuttle's Chromium never fires the lazy RSC requests', told the user 'I have to stop and hand this back to you', then twenty minutes later: 'Found it - document.hidden === true... That was the whole bug - a background tab, not a cuttle limitation.'
clustered_issues.root_cause: cuttle's base Chrome args omit Playwright's four backgrounding switches, and playwright's noDefaults:true attach path (the connectOverCDP path cuttle documents) skips Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled. The per-page pin shipped in v0.11.4 restores compositing but does not make document.visibilityState 'visible', so IntersectionObserver lazy loaders still never fire, and long-hidden tabs still degrade to ~1fps (a 220ms click becomes 3000ms).
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Extend the pin to page-visibility, pass the renderer anti-backgrounding launch flags, and expose per-target foreground/visibilityState in `cuttle status` - plus an error when Input is dispatched at a target that cannot receive it, instead of silence.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: 139 timeouts corpus-wide plus each one's retry ladder; single worst session 58 calls and a task handed back to the user.

clustered_issues.issue: cuttle's own focus pin poisons `document.hasFocus()`, so the standard focus diagnostic an agent reaches for returns true while input is not being routed to the target at all.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S06 at 15:35:44, after page.bringToFront(): `{"hasFocus": true, "steps": "VALID 0", "cmd": "[]", "cmdChk": "VALID 0"}` - the insert still did nothing. A minute earlier a force-click had reported `{"focused":"dark | BODY"}`. Agent: 'The document has focus but insertText isn't working, which is strange since it worked earlier.' It cycled five theories over ~10 calls and published a root cause its own evidence contradicts.
clustered_issues.root_cause: Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled makes hasFocus() report true regardless of real input routing, so a cuttle feature silently invalidates the one introspectable focus signal agents have.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: A truthful `cuttle status --focus` / `whoami-tab` reporting which target actually receives Input, and a SKILL.md line stating that under cuttle hasFocus() and visibilityState do not predict input delivery.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~10 calls and one wrong published diagnosis.

clustered_issues.issue: Tabs are addressed by positional integer in a browser other actors freely mutate, so every index an agent memorizes goes stale - there is no agent-owned tab, no stable handle, and no cuttle tab verb at all.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S17: an eval landed on the human's own tab and returned `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<', "<!doctype "... is not valid JSON` - twice - and the compaction summary had to carry 'my tab is tab 1, tab 0 is HIS' as standing state, which inverted when the human closed a tab. S15: `tab-close 3; tab-close 1; tab-close 0` in one command left four tabs with reshuffled indices. S05: an eval intended for a Notion dialog executed against a a SaaS console page and returned a React stack trace the agent did not recognise as wrong-page output. S07: every driver result dumped nine unrelated tabs the agent had to reason about.
clustered_issues.root_cause: cuttle exposes no tab/target concept - enumeration only arrives as a driver side effect, indices are positional, and cuttle's own immortal keep-alive about:blank tab occupies an ordinal that shifts everything after it.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle open --name <label>` returning a stable target id, `cuttle tabs` listing id/url/title/foreground/owner, and driver commands pinnable to an id (or an `--expect-url` guard that fails rather than executing against whatever is at that ordinal now).
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~115 calls corpus-wide by one audit's count; 33 calls (18%) in a single session spent only on tab orientation.

clustered_issues.issue: Every attach inherits whatever page the last human or agent left focused - including expired banking sessions and unrelated signup pages - so the agent's first automatic snapshot is often of somebody else's work.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S27: attach landed on `0: (current) [](https://a media-index site/signup.php)` and auto-snapshotted it. S15: `0: [Logout - a consumer banking web app](.../a session-timeout page)`, `3: [a consumer banking app](https://a consumer banking web app/logged-out)` - expired sessions that look like live logins in a tab list. S16's audit: 'playwright-cli attach defaults its current tab to index 0 - the user's tab, usually not foreground - so it fires on the very first command for most users.'
clustered_issues.root_cause: Attach binds to the browser's focused tab. The persistent profile accumulates stale tabs from finished tasks and there is no hygiene or agent-scoped starting point.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Hand each attaching client a dedicated working tab (or document `tab-new` as a mandatory first step in the briefing), plus idle tab hygiene so finished tasks do not leave logged-out pages lying around.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: 2-3 orientation calls per session, ~25 corpus-wide, plus at least two wrong-page snapshots.

clustered_issues.issue: Multiple clients share one browser with no visibility, ownership, or lock - a human or a second agent silently clobbers the agent's work, and the error surfaced always blames the selector.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S05 and S06 ran against the SAME container at the same time on 2026-08-07 and were each other's invisible saboteur. S05: 'Stopping here - we're both driving the same browser and it's clobbering the work. The Notion developers tab is gone from the tab list and there are now two a SaaS console tabs, so the dialog I'd filled is closed. That also explains the three Create connection clicks that did nothing' - the task was handed back to the human. S06: 'another session has opened tabs in this browser and stolen document focus, which makes execCommand a no-op' - after it had already corrupted a live build config into `[v0.14.6 array][v0.14.5 array]`. S12 found the deployment-scale version: local dev and prod compute the same deterministic seed and land on the same single-replica Chrome, 'either side's browser.close() can kill the other's page'.
clustered_issues.root_cause: cuttle multiplexes CDP but exposes no notion of who else is attached or which targets are claimed. Seeds are a small deterministic pool with no per-client namespacing, and `cuttle status` says nothing about attached clients. cuttle's own `--context` feature exists and was never mentioned in the briefing nor used by any session.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Per-attach target ownership or an advisory lease, an attached-client count and foreground owner in `cuttle status`, per-client seed namespacing, and a briefing line telling an agent to claim a context when another session may be driving.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~50 calls plus two fully-filled forms lost, one corrupted live config, one task abandoned to the human, and the corpus's only user interrupt.

clustered_issues.issue: Actions report success with no post-condition check: clicks, fills, saves and even HTTP 200 API writes silently change nothing, so agents invent a bespoke verification loop after every single mutation.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S01 built an out-of-band protocol - Gravar -> `cuttle downloads` -> grep the form XML - after every field, because 'Q6 is confirmed still empty in the XML (the click didn't take - custom widget)'; it downloaded the same file nine times tracking Chrome's `(3).xml`...`(9).xml` counter by hand. S04: a skills PATCH 'was accepted but ignored' - HTTP 200, zero change - caught only by habit. S09: a hosting provider Submit no-op'd through three clicks and two full form refills; the cause (a 403 on /api/jwt) was found only by `ls -t .playwright-cli/console-*.log | head -1 | xargs grep -iE '403'`. S05: `el.click()` on Google's account chooser returned 'clicked account' with the URL unmoved; a bash loop over freshly-snapshotted refs printed three empty arrows and added zero pages while looking like it ran.
clustered_issues.root_cause: No layer returns a post-condition. cuttle already computes a settle gate and an aria-toggle post-click verify internally for humanized clicks and does not surface the verdict; fill/type have no equivalent at all; and drivers exit 0 on no-ops.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Every cuttle write verb returns the post-condition, not a checkmark: 'click landed, DOM unchanged, 1 request failed 403, these validation nodes became visible'; extend the existing mutation verify to fill/type and report before/after field values.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: The single largest cost in the corpus - hundreds of verification calls; S01 alone spent ~400 calls (46% of the session) answering 'what is actually on the page'.

clustered_issues.issue: There is no network or console observation verb, so agents monkey-patch window.fetch and XMLHttpRequest from inside the page, grep console log files by mtime, and download the site's own JS bundles to find out why an action failed.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S04 rewrote the page's networking stack to spy on itself: `window.fetch=async (...a)=>{...window.__net.push(o.method+' '+u+' :: '+String(o.body))...}` plus the same for XMLHttpRequest.open/send, then grepped the app's bundles from inside the page to recover an enum (`five_eight_years` -> `eight_or_more_years`) after three guessed values 400'd. S07 fetched and regexed an LWC component bundle to find a hidden 35-character address cap. S09: every result reported '183 console errors' on a professional social network, so the counter was useless as a health signal and the one real error had to be grepped out of a file. S06 could not inspect a redirect chain, substituted an in-page fetch with different cookie semantics, and wrote a wrong 'stale cache' conclusion into a committed project journal.
clustered_issues.root_cause: cuttle proxies the whole CDP Network and Runtime domains and retains none of it. Drivers expose only an unfiltered request log and a raw console-error count that large SPAs baseline in the hundreds.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle net --tail` / `cuttle console --since-last-action` per seed: failed requests with status, redirect chains with final URL, and only console entries new since the previous action, classified rather than counted.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~45 calls plus one wrong root cause persisted into a user's repo.

clustered_issues.issue: Accessibility snapshot refs are effectively single-use - they go stale on any DOM mutation and across CLI invocations - and the resulting error blames the selector rather than the staleness.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S04: `Error: Ref f6e811 not found in the current page snapshot. Try capturing new snapshot.` mid-form-fill, leaving `year_from=""`. S06: three consecutive 'Ref f13e49 not found' in one command. S05: `click f12e539` -> 'element was detached from the DOM, retrying' -> 'Ref f12e493 not found'; ref prefixes drifted e... <-> f12e... <-> f2e... between frames. S01 ran snapshot:click at exactly 1:1 (261:261) because every targeted action needed a fresh snapshot first. S27 found the same login form's refs were e35 in one session and f7e35 in another, so no known flow can be cached.
clustered_issues.root_cause: Each driver invocation is a separate process and each snapshot re-mints refs; nothing auto-refreshes or distinguishes 'ref stale' from 'element absent'.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Stable element handles that survive a re-render (or auto-resnapshot on a stale ref), plus a SKILL.md rule that refs are valid only within one chained command and role/text locators should be preferred for anything after the first action.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~40 calls of re-snapshotting, and it is the proximate reason two sessions abandoned refs for pixel coordinates entirely.

clustered_issues.issue: The accessibility snapshot omits or mislabels the controls that matter (Save buttons, OAuth links, expanders, custom Angular/LWC/a third-party site widgets), so hand-written raw-JS DOM extraction became the universal escape hatch - and the escape hatch is the move that destroys cuttle's stealth value.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S13: `snapshot | rg -i 'button.*save|publish|Save'` returned only 'Published on June 30, 2022'; a raw eval over document.querySelectorAll('button') found ' Save', and the agent pressed it with an injected `b.click()` - an isTrusted:false event the humanizer never sees. S14: ~20 of ~35 a consumer banking web app calls were raw evals because the a11y layer was useless on legacy WebForms; `type` on a 7-box OTP put the first three digits in boxes 5-7 because a ref focused the wrong input. S07: 'The form lives in a CRM platform LWC shadow DOM - document.querySelector can't see it (Playwright locators can)' - the agent hand-wrote a shadowRoot walker. S15: `find 'Continue with GitHub' | rg 'ref='` returned four nested generics and no link ref.
clustered_issues.root_cause: The a11y tree is the only structured page view cuttle's documented drivers offer, and it is lossy on exactly the widget families real authenticated apps use. There is no blessed structured-extraction path, so agents fall to page-context JS - which is blind to shadow DOM and bypasses humanization.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: A `cuttle extract --selector ... --format json` / state-read verb that returns form values keyed by nearest stable id/name/label and pierces shadow DOM, plus a documented rule that eval is for reads only and locators pierce shadow DOM where document.querySelector does not.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: Hundreds of calls; it is the single most-repeated workaround in the corpus and it is why isTrusted:false clicks appear in at least six sessions.

clustered_issues.issue: Reading a page is expensive and awkward: snapshots run to thousands of lines, land as timestamped YAML files in whatever directory the shell is in, and must be located with `ls -t` and mined with rg/sed line windows.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S28 reconstructed a 27-name guest list with `f=$(ls -t .playwright-cli/page-*.yml | head -1) && rg -n -i 'sign in|approved|guest' "$f"` then `sed -n '190,352p' "$f" | rg -o 'Profile picture for ([^"]+)"'`. S30 needed seven shell calls to read one a professional social network profile: snapshot -> ls -t the YAML -> rg -> sed -> run-code scroll -> snapshot -> rg. S13 grep-and-sed'd snapshots ~12 times, once getting nothing back from `sed -n '150,260p'` with no idea what part of the page it had sliced. S20 read a billing page as `document.body.innerText.split('\n').slice(18,60)` - magic-number offsets into a text dump.
clustered_issues.root_cause: No scoped, token-budgeted read primitive. The a11y snapshot is all-or-nothing, is written to disk by the driver rather than returned, and agents therefore only ever see the slice they already suspected mattered.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle read [--selector] [--region dialog] [--text|--aria]` returning a context-sized extract inline, and a stable artifact location that is not the user's cwd.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~60 calls, plus the systematic risk of reasoning from a slice chosen before the answer was known.

clustered_issues.issue: The dominant real use of cuttle is authenticated data extraction - a tab that carries the user's cookies - and it has no verb, so every session independently reverse-engineers the site's private API and re-derives its auth flow from scratch.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: The identical incantation appears in S23, S37, S29, S33, S27 and S34: `--raw eval "async () => { const t=(await (await fetch('https://api.a freelance marketplace/auth/refresh-token',{method:'POST',credentials:'include'})).json()).token; const r=await fetch('https://api.a freelance marketplace/missions/open/v2',{headers:{Authorization:'Bearer '+t}}); return await r.text(); }" | jq`. S17 spent 24 of 29 calls on in-page fetch of a link-aggregator site .json because 'plain curl is bot-blocked', and carried the 400-character shell-quoted blob as session state across three compactions. S02's user pushed back directly: 'every time i ask you to check a professional social network, do you need to run cuttle for that? could you store the token in here somehow and use voyager api only to do quick checks for me?' In three cuttle sessions (S36, S37, S40) not one CDP input event was ever sent - zero clicks, zero typing.
clustered_issues.root_cause: cuttle's value today is 'a logged-in cookie jar reachable over CDP', and its briefing names drivers and attach commands but never names this use case. Everything above that layer is the agent's own JS, re-derived per session and per site.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle fetch <url> [--json] [--out file]` and `cuttle eval --file script.js` executing in the seed's authenticated page context, returning un-escaped output and streaming large results to a file. This is the most-used capability in the batch and the only one with no verb.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: Re-derivation cost paid in ~15 sessions; one recurring job measured at 24 calls / 11.6 min before codification and 2 calls / 47s after.

clustered_issues.issue: Getting a file out of the browser is one-directional and brittle: `cuttle downloads` needs an exact filename with no --latest, and there is no way to capture a resource the site renders inline instead of downloading.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S01 tracked Chrome's dedup counter by hand across the session - `(3).xml` through `(9).xml` - listing the download directory whenever it lost count; when a PDF opened in a viewer tab instead of downloading, `cuttle downloads` reported nothing and the agent wrote `page.evaluate('async () => { const r = await fetch(...); const b = await r.blob(); const a = document.createElement(...)')` to synthesize a download it could then retrieve. S02 needed three navigations to surface a full-res image URL it could then fetch.
clustered_issues.root_cause: The downloads surface only serves files Chrome happened to write, addressed by exact name; authenticated resources rendered in-page have no capture path.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle downloads --latest` / glob support, and `cuttle grab <url> [dest]` performing an in-profile authenticated fetch that writes bytes host-side.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~50 calls in the one session that leaned on downloads as its verification channel.

clustered_issues.issue: There is no upload path into the containerized browser: the driver's upload verb is gated on an already-armed file chooser, fails silently when it is not, and nobody documents whether a path resolves on the host or in the container.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S07 simply never tried - 'On the documents: yes, there was an upload field, and I missed it' - and by the time the human asked ('and wasn't there any place in form to submit docs?') the wizard had locked the a national tax id with `attachmentsJSON: ""`, forcing the document out of band by email. S02 ran `docker cp /tmp/kc-logo.png cuttle:/tmp/...`, then `agent-browser upload` reported success while a hand-written probe returned `{files:0}`; only `page.setInputFiles` with a Mac path worked, making the docker cp dead work. S04 got `Error: The tool "browser_file_upload" can only be used when there is related modal state present`, then guessed a control and fired a PDF at the cover-image uploader on the user's live account. S01 hit both errors in mirror image, including a snapshot that refused to run at all: 'Tool browser_snapshot does not handle the modal state.'
clustered_issues.root_cause: cuttle owns the downloads direction and not its mirror. Upload is a per-driver behaviour keyed to modal state, with no way to name the target input and no documented path-resolution rule for a browser that runs in a container.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle upload <selector-or-index> <local-file>` that stages the file and sets it via CDP DOM.setFileInputFiles regardless of modal state and returns the file name and byte count as the page sees it, plus one SKILL.md line stating which side paths resolve on.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~45 calls plus one permanently incomplete legal filing and one wrong-widget upload on a live account.

clustered_issues.issue: The container boundary is undocumented in both directions: host file paths and host localhost are invisible to the browser, so agents guess addresses, docker cp defensively, or rebind the user's dev server.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S02 first opened `http://host.docker.internal:4321/` then flip-flopped to the LAN address `http://<lan-ip>:4321/`; later in the same session it killed the user's dev server and restarted it with `pnpm dev --host` purely so the containerized browser could reach it, hardcoding a machine-specific IP into a dozen subsequent calls. A separate session (S19) drove a browser 27 times against http://localhost:5173 and never touched cuttle at all, because a host dev server is unreachable from the container and nothing flags it.
clustered_issues.root_cause: cuttle runs the browser in Docker and says nothing about the network or filesystem boundary, so the exact workflow cuttle should own - verify your local UI change in a real browser - silently routes around it.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: A documented, stable in-container hostname for the host (and whether the daemon adds the host-gateway mapping), or a `cuttle open --host-port 4321` that sets up the forward; plus a line stating host paths are not visible to the browser.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~20 calls plus one session's browser state stranded in a second unmanaged profile.

clustered_issues.issue: The driver's secrets file binds at attach time, so an unknown secret name is typed literally into the field with no error - a failure that perfectly mimics truncation and has already put placeholder strings into live password fields.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S08: `fill f7e182 HC_PASS` returned 'len=7' with no warning; a 24-char control secret landed as len=11. The agent concluded 'The secret-substitution path drops characters - a driver bug, not the site' and aborted the whole task to a human handoff, before finding the truth: 'HC_PASS is 7 characters, TEST_SECRET is 11 - exactly the lengths that landed. Nothing was truncated; it typed the literal variable names, because the secrets file is read by the daemon at attach time.' S01 hit the same thing on a government tax portal - `fill(...'PF_PASS')` produced 'Campo demasiado pequeno' - and the user ended up typing his own password: [user expressed frustration and entered the credentials manually]. S04's TOTP expired between mint and submit because a fresh secret needs a fresh attach - it accumulated sessions bt, bt2, bt3 against one browser in 90 seconds.
clustered_issues.root_cause: Secret substitution is a driver env-var feature evaluated once at session create. Nothing verifies redaction is armed on an already-attached session, nothing errors on an unknown name, and a time-bounded secret cannot be refreshed without a new attach.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: cuttle-owned secret injection resolved at use time (`cuttle secret set NAME --from-command 'op item get ... --otp'`, `cuttle type --secret NAME`), with a hard error on an unknown name and an affordance to check whether redaction is armed.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~35 calls, two human credential takeovers, one wrongly-aborted task, and two burned TOTP attempts.

clustered_issues.issue: cuttle owns no secret-injection path, so three separate sessions independently reinvented the same undocumented native-value-setter + base64 DOM hack to type a password - and that path cannot reach run-code at all, making the efficient path and the safe path mutually exclusive.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: The identical incantation in S23, S26, S27 and S33: `const setter=Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(window.HTMLInputElement.prototype,'value').set; setter.call(inp, atob('$(printenv ATEAM_PASSWORD | base64)').trim()); inp.dispatchEvent(new Event('input',{bubbles:true}))` - which also skips real key events, so the Sign In button stays `[disabled]` and has to be force-clicked. S16's audit established the complementary hole: 'playwright-cli's secrets substitution doesn't work inside run-code at all (no process.env in the sandbox)', so a batched script can only hold a secret by inlining the literal into argv where redaction cannot reach it. S11 did exactly that with a live OTP: `run-code "async page => { await page.keyboard.type('<otp>', { delay: 150 }); }"`.
clustered_issues.root_cause: The only secrets mechanism lives in one driver, applies only to its discrete fill/type verbs, and is disabled by the batched style that same stack's performance characteristics push agents toward. cuttle knows exactly what it typed and owns none of it.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Daemon-owned secret injection at the CDP Input layer - a named secret any driver can reference in any call shape, delivered as real keystrokes, never crossing argv, the transcript, or driver output.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: Re-derived in at least 4 sessions; the user's own CLAUDE.md now encodes the hazard as a rule ('never in fill or run-code', 'don't snapshot between fill and submit').

clustered_issues.issue: Redaction is driver-side, all-or-nothing and destructive: it shreds unrelated output when secrets are short, blocks reading legitimate page data, and secrets still leak through snapshots, navigation URLs in driver logs, and the transcript.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S26: `snapshot | grep -iE 'error|textbox'` returned `- textbox "Password..." [ref=e28]: t2J6bXyCQumuF!cukv` - the standard way to diagnose a failed login is a credential exfiltration path. S14 produced a real incident requiring rotation: with per-digit secrets loaded, output came back as `Console: <secret>MBCP_MC_<secret>MBCP_MC_5</secret></secret> errors` and even refs were redacted (`textbox "5ª" [ref=e<secret>MBCP_P5</secret>]`), so the agent detached to read the page - and that snapshot printed three of the user's seven multicanal digits in plaintext. In the same session the human's SMS OTP entered the transcript because there is no hand-in path, and S08 had a live session key leak through a routine driver retry log: '- retrying click action - waiting for "https://z-library.sk/?remix_userid=...&remix_userkey=25039df9..." navigation to finish'.
clustered_issues.root_cause: Redaction is a naive global substring replace over all driver output, armed once at attach. It is simultaneously too broad (destroys refs, timestamps, counts) and too narrow (does not cover snapshots' input values or URLs the driver echoes).
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Daemon-side, value-scoped, always-on masking of exactly the values cuttle injected, plus snapshot-side redaction of password/one-time-code inputs and credential-shaped URL params - and a `cuttle secret prompt` so a human can hand over an OTP without it entering the transcript.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~15 calls plus one credential rotation, one exposed session key, and two OTPs in plaintext.

clustered_issues.issue: Humanized typing is too slow for bulk or long text, so every agent independently invents an insertText/JS bypass - and the bypass has an undocumented 80-rune cliff above which the value lands with zero keystrokes.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S01's 33-row IBAN loop ran 16:19:54 -> 16:24:26 for ~950 characters, and the BIC column could not be filled at all, so the agent edited the XML offline and re-uploaded - which then triggered the Leave-site dialog and wiped the live draft. S10 wrote .js files to route a 3386-char body through `page.keyboard.insertText`, i.e. 'the fields that most need to look human were filled by the least human path'. S22 refused to type a 1049-character appeal at all and hand-built a run-code fill. S16 measured the cliff: 'short (16) -> 2537ms, 159ms/char; at cap (80) -> 11996ms, 150ms/char; over cap (140) -> 8ms, 0ms/char.'
clustered_issues.root_cause: ~130-160ms/char with an 80-rune cap and a silent fallback to a single unhumanized edit. Nothing documents the arithmetic, the cap, or when the bypass is safe, so agents rediscover it and pick the wrong side by accident.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: A blessed bulk-text/paste path with a stated stealth tradeoff (chunked humanized runs, or an explicit opt-out per command), and a daemon warning when a fill silently falls back to insertText so the agent knows the property was not applied.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~45 calls plus several minutes of blocking wall clock per long field.

clustered_issues.issue: Humanized typing outruns the driver's fixed 5s action timeout, producing a hard TimeoutError on a write that actually succeeded - on live accounts, where the naive retry duplicates the text.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S11, twice on the user's live profile: 'TimeoutError: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. Call log: - waiting for locator(aria-ref=f3e742) - fill("Co-Founder, Baton (current US client, contract via a freelance marketplace)") - attempting fill action' - 56 characters. The agent's message: 'The fills actually landed (humanized typing just outran the CLI's 5s report window)', and it recorded the rule as 'verify via snapshot, don't retry blindly'.
clustered_issues.root_cause: Nothing negotiates the driver's default action timeout against cuttle's per-character pacing, and the arithmetic (chars x ~130ms) is documented nowhere. An agent that trusts the error doubles the text; one that aborts leaves a half-filled form.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: cuttle extends or negotiates the attached driver's action timeout when humanization is on; failing that, SKILL.md must state the arithmetic and the rule 'on a fill timeout, read back before retrying - never re-fill'.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: 4 calls, but the highest-risk friction in the batch: a false failure on a live-account write.

clustered_issues.issue: Humanization is baked at `cuttle up` and cannot be toggled at runtime, so an agent that discovers it is doing bulk entry on the user's own logged-in account can only opt out by recreating the container and destroying the warm session.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S04 paid ~0.5s/click for ~50 interactions on the user's own a freelance marketplace profile - five minutes just to remove and re-add ~30 skill chips one at a time - with no adversary at all; humanize is listed among the baked flags, so switching it off means --recreate, i.e. discarding a session that cost a password, two failed TOTP attempts and four attach cycles. S01 never even considered the flag because the draft it was filling existed only client-side. S03 found the inverse problem: 'v0.10.0 turned server-side input humanization on by default, and we still call humanizeBrowser client-side. Unmeasured interaction' - resolved by guessing.
clustered_issues.root_cause: The humanize decision must be made before the agent knows what kind of work the task is, and revising it destroys the thing that makes cuttle valuable. There is also no way to observe whether input is being humanized server-side, so double-humanization cannot be measured.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Per-connection or per-command humanize control (e.g. `?humanize=0` on the CDP attach URL, alongside the existing `?fingerprint=`) plus humanize state reported in `cuttle status` and the attach briefing.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: Several minutes of wall clock per session, unquantified but systematic.

clustered_issues.issue: The humanization boundary is narrow and invisible: the humanizer intercepts only Input.dispatchMouseEvent/dispatchKeyEvent, so fill/insertText and every raw-eval write bypass it silently - and SKILL.md claimed the opposite.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S16 measured before/after on live containers: 0.11.3 `fill()` took 15-19ms with **0 keydowns**; 0.11.4 took 1.1s with **10 keydowns** for the identical value - the prefilter at humanize.go:357 matched only 'Input.dispatch' so insertText never decoded. The same audit: 'anything going through Runtime.evaluate bypasses humanization entirely AND produces isTrusted=false' - while SKILL.md:199-206 claimed typing was 'rewritten into human-paced motion'. S01 shows the scale: 65 of its eval calls performed the actual clicks and typing via .click()/dispatchEvent/nativeInputValueSetter, none of which the daemon ever sees.
clustered_issues.root_cause: The humanizer sits on two CDP methods and everything else routes around it, with no signal to the caller. The doc asserting otherwise made agents believe box.fill(txt) was the humanized path.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Report humanization coverage per action (or warn when a page mutates without dispatched Input), and keep SKILL.md's behavioural claims under test against the daemon's actual code paths.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: Silent - which is what makes it dangerous; at least one wrong stealth decision in a live session.

clustered_issues.issue: When the driver's click fails there is no trusted-click escape hatch, so agents escalate to force-click, DOM dispatchEvent, or hand-computed coordinates - the exact move that emits isTrusted:false and throws away the product's whole reason to exist.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S07 adopted dispatchEvent as its reflex before catching itself: 'synthetic events are isTrusted: false, while cuttle's humanized input layer sends real CDP input events... Making dispatchEvent my reflex quietly throws away the stealth property on exactly the anti-bot sites where we need it.' S05 rebuilt clicking from scratch: 27 evals whose only job was getBoundingClientRect, each followed by `mousemove X Y; mousedown; mouseup` - two calls per click, coordinates stale on any reflow. S09: 'roughly 30 of the 64 driver calls are --raw eval DOM surgery, including every Submit click'. S13 pressed a Save button with an injected `b.click()` because no ref existed. S05 also proved the cost: `el.click()` on Google's account chooser returned 'clicked account' and the URL never moved; only a real mouse press advanced it.
clustered_issues.root_cause: cuttle's humanized input is only reachable through a driver verb that frequently cannot resolve or act on the element, and no cuttle-native alternative exists, so the only escape hatch available is the one that defeats humanization.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle click <selector|x,y>` that resolves, scrolls into view, foregrounds the target and dispatches humanized real Input in one call - plus a hard SKILL.md rule that dispatchEvent/force-click through cuttle is forbidden, paired with that alternative.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~80 calls of coordinate arithmetic and dispatch escalation, and a systematic stealth regression cuttle cannot currently see.

clustered_issues.issue: The driver's actionability check ('visible, enabled and stable') never settles on animated SPA and consent UIs, so agents burn 5s and 30s timeouts and then abandon the high-level verbs permanently for the rest of the session.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S06: `click e50` -> 'TimeoutError: Timeout 5000ms exceeded ... locator resolved to <button ...>' twice, then the same on a role locator; the agent told the user proactively 'a SaaS console buttons never pass Playwright's stability check (some persistent animation), so I'm clicking via DOM dispatch'. S07 on a OneTrust banner: 'waiting for element to be visible, enabled and stable' -> ~4 failed calls. S02: 223 eval/run-code calls against 4 clicks, with the user forcing a driver switch - 'i hope it would be faster and less error-prone' - and the agent conceding 'agent-browser was clearly the better tool here'. S05's Google consent flow: two ref/role clicks timed out and the entire remainder of the OAuth flow ran on raw coordinates.
clustered_issues.root_cause: A stability heuristic designed for static pages, applied to perpetually-animating marketing and consent UIs, with a bare timeout that names the element rather than the reason. cuttle's briefing lists drivers 'in priority order' with no routing guidance about when the default is a bad fit.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: SKILL.md naming this failure mode with the exact remedy, a symptom-to-driver routing hint ('two consecutive actionability timeouts on an animated SPA -> switch driver, same browser, no state lost'), and a cuttle-side click that keeps trusted input while skipping the driver's stability gate.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~50 calls plus ~2 minutes of pure timeout wall clock, and two sessions that never used a high-level verb again.

clustered_issues.issue: Widget-specific input semantics differ invisibly (masked inputs append instead of replacing, React-controlled inputs ignore type but accept fill, tag/chip inputs need a commit gesture, multi-box OTPs mis-focus, sliders and CodeMirror ignore programmatic sets) and none of it is documented.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S01: campo 61 was AT-prefilled with 9,81; the agent typed 9,81 and the field became 9.819,81 on a legally-binding tax form - caught only by the human. S14: `fill '#dtEnd' '10/08/2026'` read back as '25/06/2026 .. 10/08/2026/08/2026'. S04: 'type f6e1208 "Rust"' produced no options, `fill` on the same ref did. S05 spent 20 calls and 12 strategies committing one tag-input chip, solved only by a hand-written 5-event MouseEvent chain. S06's CodeMirror writes degraded from replace to append and produced invalid JSON two clicks from being saved as live build config.
clustered_issues.root_cause: No layer reads the field back, and no doc carries the per-widget rules that every real authenticated app needs. Each failure produces a syntactically plausible wrong value rather than an error.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Report the field's before/after value on every fill/type (the single change that converts this whole class from invisible to obvious), plus a short 'modern form widgets' section in SKILL.md covering masked, controlled, chip, multi-box and rich-text inputs.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~60 calls plus two near-miss writes of wrong data to live systems.

clustered_issues.issue: There is no wait-for-condition primitive, so agents pad every action with blind sleeps and hand-roll polling loops - over an hour of wall clock across the window, and 'is it stuck or just slow' is never answerable.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S06: 32 sleeps totalling 894s plus 7 hand-rolled polling loops (~40 min), including `for i in 1..8; do sleep 40; playwright-cli goto ".../tests/<id>?p=$i"` and one attempt rejected outright by the harness ('Blocked: sleep 150 followed by: curl'). S05: 85 of 183 browser calls contain a literal sleep, 354s total, values 1-8s. S04: 76 sleeps (~264s) despite SKILL.md's own rule 'Never sleep; wait for a condition' - because it had navigated inside eval, which leaves no driver-side navigation to wait on. S16's corpus figure: 'Blind sleeps cost >1 hour of wall-clock across the window (one session: 58% of calls had a hardcoded sleep).'
clustered_issues.root_cause: No wait primitive at the cuttle layer and no confidence in the drivers'; combined with humanized latency and cold starts, agents cannot distinguish designed slowness from a hang, so they guess a duration on every interaction. Several sessions also had to append cache-busting query params (?v=1, ?p=$i) because there is no hard-reload verb.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle wait --tab N --until '<js predicate>' | --url-matches | --settled --timeout`, a documented hard-reload, and a stated per-action latency budget so agents stop padding humanized clicks with 9-second sleeps.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: >1 hour of pure wall-clock sleeping corpus-wide, plus ~60 polling calls.

clustered_issues.issue: Every driver verb pays 0.25-0.8s of CLI process startup regardless of the browser, making discrete-verb loops expensive - and the batching workaround then breaks on stale refs and non-atomic scripts.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S16 timed it: attach 498ms, tab-list 235ms, and 10 Hacker News rows extracted in 33ms in one batched call versus ~797ms per discrete eval round trip - 'That's CLI process startup dominating'. S21 batched `click e516 && click e533 && click e558 && click e580` to amortize ~7s-per-click latency and the later refs died on mutations the earlier clicks caused. S06 retried a run-code script whose first half had already clicked Submit, and hit 'TimeoutError: locator.evaluate ... waiting for getByRole("button", { name: "Submit for Review" })' against a dialog that was already gone. S05 read the driver SKILL.md, never used run-code once in 183 calls, and its own audit put ~65 of those calls as collapsible to ~5.
clustered_issues.root_cause: A per-invocation process model plus a ref system valid for exactly one action, so the two obvious efficiency moves (batch; reuse refs) are mutually incompatible and run-code errors do not report how far a script got.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: A persistent-session read/act path at the cuttle layer, and SKILL.md stating the batching rule and its counter-rule (batch reads, not clicks; re-find refs inside the batch; run-code is not atomic).
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: A corpus-wide multiplier on every session's call count.

clustered_issues.issue: There is no wait-for-login or handoff primitive: the agent parks a page, prints the viewer URL in prose, and ends its turn - resuming only when the human types 'done'.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S18 stalled ~36 hours on GitHub sudo mode and hand-wrote its own waiter: `for i in $(seq 1 90); do t=$(playwright-cli --raw eval "document.title"); if [ "$t" != "Confirm access" ]; then echo "page advanced"; exit 0; fi; sleep 4; done`. S20 parked a a crypto exchange console 2FA tab and idled ~10 minutes. S06 idled 12 minutes and the user sent two near-identical 'i did the auth, continue' messages. S36 wrote a site-specific `fetch('/api/retail/user/current/wallet')` probe just to answer 'is this origin still authenticated', then ended its turn waiting for 'its logged in'.
clustered_issues.root_cause: The VNC viewer is cuttle's flagship handoff feature and no verb uses it. There is no login-state probe before the wall and no completion signal after it, so every agent rebuilds the protocol out of shell loops and prose.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle handoff <url> --until <predicate> --timeout` that opens the page, prints the exact viewer link focused on the right tab, notifies the human, and returns when the page leaves the sign-in origin - plus `cuttle auth status <domain>` for the before half.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~25 calls plus ~36h, ~12min and ~10min of wall-clock stalls in three separate sessions.

clustered_issues.issue: The VNC viewer is essentially never reached for even at the exact moments it exists for, and once it was reached for wrongly - the skill names no triggers for handoff.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S04 hit a 2FA login AND walked up to an irreversible Delete on the user's live resume without ever offering the viewer; the human intervened out-of-band by driving the browser himself ('i just updated the resume on resume tab myself'). S05 never opened or mentioned the viewer in 183 calls despite `cuttle up` having printed it, including at the moment it handed the task back to the human. S10 guided the human click-by-click through a professional social network report dialogs from memory, getting the labels wrong three times, while the human pasted a screenshot at every step ('i don't want to guess options all the time'). Conversely S08 aborted to the viewer for two password fields it could have typed itself; the user: 'read cuttle's skill and check full playwright-cli skill / you should be able to do that yourself!'
clustered_issues.root_cause: SKILL.md markets the viewer but sets no bar for invoking it, so handoff is neither reached for when it is right (captcha, 2FA, destructive action on a live account, human-drives-while-agent-watches) nor excluded when it is wrong (typing a password).
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Explicit handoff triggers in SKILL.md (real captcha/2FA/bank step/irreversible action - not 'typing a password'), and a verb that opens the viewer at the current tab so offering it costs one call.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~20 calls plus multiple human takeovers and one wrongly-aborted task.

clustered_issues.issue: Handoff is one-directional: when the human takes the keyboard in the viewer mid-flow, nothing tells the agent, so it keeps issuing commands against a page that has already moved.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S01, three times: 'i entered <redacted-id> myself, and it just worked... you were overthinking stuff' (after 52 agent calls on that modal), 'i did mouse drag myself, check the value now' (after four failed slider strategies), and 'i entered creds myself'. Also 'did that [screenshot]. check the current page pls' - the user had to explicitly instruct the agent to re-read the page after acting in the viewer.
clustered_issues.root_cause: cuttle sits between the viewer and the browser and could see human-originated input, but exposes no event or diff. Collaborative handoff - human does one thing mid-flow - is not a supported shape.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: A 'page changed by viewer input at T' signal in `cuttle status` or annotated on the next driver result, plus SKILL.md guidance to re-read state after asking the human to do one step.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~20 calls issued against a stale model of the page.

clustered_issues.issue: The advertised 'logins persist across down/up' is not true for the sites that matter, and there is no way to ask whether a seed is still authenticated - so every session opens by re-running the risky login flow.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: All three a freelance marketplace board checks (S23 Aug 6, S27 Aug 10, S33 Aug 12) opened logged out despite the persistent profile and 3008-cookie state snapshots visible in the daemon log; the agent has internalized it - 'Logged out as expected (their sessions always expire)' - and the user's workflow docs now open with 'ASSUME LOGGED OUT'. S01 found the server-side variant: 'The one thing that actually was broken: your server session had expired. Clicking Entregar an hour ago would have bounced you to the login page and wiped the draft.' S15 attached into a browser holding a timed-out a consumer banking web app tab and a logged-out a consumer banking app that both look like live logins in a tab list.
clustered_issues.root_cause: The cookie jar persists; the server-side session does not, and cuttle's briefing promise reads stronger than reality. Nothing surfaces per-origin auth state, so the only detector is landing on a sign-in redirect - which then drags the unsupported password flow along with it.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle auth status [origin]` reporting which origins have stored cookies, when state was captured, and how old it is - and a SKILL.md line stating that persisted cookies do not mean a live server session.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: 3-5 calls per session as a fixed tax, plus the login flow (and its credential risk) paid repeatedly.

clustered_issues.issue: Session state is lost silently by four independent routes that all return err == nil: capture reads only the default context, an empty capture overwrites a good snapshot before the profile is deleted, idle reap discards the profile because --keep-profile defaults false, and hand-rolled deployments omit the volume the CLI sets.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S03, found by source review not by failing: 'storage.GetCookies() is called with no BrowserContextID, so it resolves to the default context only... a capture that returns err == nil (so the if !ok bail never fires), overwrites the prior good snapshot last-writer-wins, and then pool.go:628 deletes the profile dir. Cookies for that context are lost on every capture; its localStorage *is* captured, so the snapshot is left internally inconsistent.' S12's audit: 'browser.newContext() creates an incognito context... Cuttle's own code says its restore path cannot reach it' plus '/data on no volume in either compose or helm' - i.e. the advertised persistent-logins feature was quietly inert in production. S02 shows the human-visible version: raw-HTTP testing invalidated the a professional social network session and re-login had to be improvised and documented privately.
clustered_issues.root_cause: Every loss path is invisible at the moment it happens, and the standard driver call (browser.newContext) puts pages exactly where capture and restore cannot see them.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Union cookies across all contexts, refuse to overwrite a good snapshot with an empty one, and warn at the point of loss - 'your login will not survive because X' - including when a client creates a context the restore path cannot reach or when a reap discards a profile.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: Unquantifiable because it is silent; one live a professional social network login burned and re-authenticated through VNC.

clustered_issues.issue: `cuttle up` silently restarts and discards the tab set with no reason given, and --recreate's effect on the persistent profile is ambiguous enough that the agent had to verify it with raw docker commands.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S40: `cuttle up` returned 'cuttle **restarted**' and the browser came back with only about:blank - the same command printed 'already running' / 'running' in two other sessions - with no reason and no warning that the human's logged-in tabs were gone. S07: the user rejected the agent's `cuttle down; cuttle up` and asked for --recreate, at which point the agent said 'One caveat worth checking first: --recreate only keeps your logins if the profile is a named volume (the status text from the older image says it discards the profile)' and fell back to `docker volume ls` and `docker inspect`. S06 could not attribute tab loss at all: 'your logged-in tabs were dropped when the browser restarted mid-session, not by me.'
clustered_issues.root_cause: The lifecycle verbs report outcome without cause, and the help/status text about profile handling is stale and self-contradictory in a user whose browser habitually holds human-opened tabs.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: State the restart reason and warn that the tab set was discarded; make --recreate print which profile volume it re-attaches; and offer a `cuttle ensure` that attaches to a healthy container and refuses to recreate unless asked.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~6 calls plus silent loss of a human's browsing state.

clustered_issues.issue: `Target.createBrowserContext` is blocked with a message that names no escape hatch, and the caller is usually third-party library code the operator cannot patch - it took down a whole production browser tier.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S03: the failure reached the client as a truncated `502 ... {"error": "Browser.new_context: Protocol error (Target.createBrowserContext): Target.createBrowserContext is blocked by cuttle: one identity per seed - attach to the existing default context, or start` - cut off mid-sentence, six times. 'There is no opt-out flag or env var - I grepped for one.' The remedy in the message is addressed to whoever wrote the CDP call, but 'scrapling inside scraping-py calls Browser.new_context internally. That is third-party code we don't control.' The user redirected the entire task: 'lets instead of changing anything on the side of this project - go and make ~/pj/cuttle/ fully compatible first'. S16 hit the same wall later and had to `cuttle up --help | rg -i allow-context` to find the flag.
clustered_issues.root_cause: A protocol-level block shipped without a documented opt-out on day one, with a remedy sentence aimed at the wrong audience and long enough to be truncated by every error-wrapping layer above it.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Lead the rejection with the actionable token in the first 80 characters ('set --allow-context-creation / CUTTLE_ALLOW_CONTEXT_CREATION=1 if your driver cannot attach'), and a compatibility section in SKILL.md listing which stacks call newContext internally.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~15 diagnosis calls plus an entire release cycle (implement, review, 319-test gate, image build, canary).

clustered_issues.issue: There is no readiness gate: startup returns before CDP serves, so agents hand-roll `sleep 12` plus curl polling - and one session bypassed the cuttle CLI entirely, running 13 `docker run -d` and 21 defensive `docker rm -f` to reimplement port and readiness handling badly.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S44 ran `docker compose --profile dev up -d cuttle | tail -2 && sleep 12 && curl -sS -m 5 http://127.0.0.1:24022/json/version` and later diagnosed itself: 'docker compose up -d returns when containers are created, not when they're serving - which is exactly why I ended up writing sleep 12 and curl-polling /json/version by hand'; the human's correction was blunt - 'it feels like you keep falling back to docker compose directly in most occasions' - and the cost was skipping `cuttle-smoke`, the exact check for the browser path being regression-tested. S03 made 413 Bash calls with ZERO `cuttle up`/`down`/`open` and 27 cold-start sleeps totalling 602s.
clustered_issues.root_cause: The lifecycle verbs are documented in human-shaped terms while the tool agents reach for has a `-d` flag that fits a tool-call loop. Nothing blocks until the first Chrome is attachable and nothing exits non-zero until it is.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle up --wait` / `cuttle status --json` with a ready boolean and a non-zero exit until ready, documented as a non-interactive command sequence with a readiness gate and an exit code - including for the --image testing path.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~60 calls and ~10 minutes of pure cold-start sleeping in one session alone.

clustered_issues.issue: cuttle exposes no machine-readable self-description - persona, arch, effective config, humanize state, viewport, daemon version, idle timeout, bind scope - so every consumer hand-rolls detection and green results carry no information about what was actually exercised.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S12 discovered arm64=macOS / amd64=Windows only by querying /json/version ('Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7' locally, 'Windows NT 10.0' on the cluster) and then added a persona line to its harness 'so it can never claim a path it didn't run'; a related build-smoke assertion 'passes vacuously under the macOS persona'. It also had to diff local vs prod by hand: arm64/macOS vs amd64/Windows, /dev/shm 3GB vs 2Gi, --idle-timeout 90 vs 600. S03 mis-pinned an arm64 digest and the only feedback was `exec /usr/bin/tini: exec format error`. S16: `cuttle up --image ...:0.11.3` printed the CLI's version 0.11.4 on the ready line during an A/B whose whole point was which daemon build was running.
clustered_issues.root_cause: Everything meaningful about a running cuttle is inferable only by attaching a browser and reading navigator, or by reading two deployment systems side by side. `cuttle status` reports neither the daemon's own version nor its effective configuration.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle status --json` reporting readiness, daemon version, persona, arch, effective flags (humanize, idle-timeout, shm), per-seed window/viewport, reachable CDP address and bind scope - one command that two instances can be diffed with.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~30 calls across the infra sessions, plus one production-shaped conclusion drawn from a local green.

clustered_issues.issue: There is no instance identity on the HTTP surface: a green TCP probe on the CDP port proves nothing about which cuttle - or whether it is cuttle at all - the driver is talking to.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S12: 'A local cuttle container still on 24022 makes the port-forward's until loop spin unable to bind while the probe goes green off the local container - so --remote-browser silently runs against the local arm64/macOS farm believing it's on cluster amd64/Windows'; the eventual fix was asserting on the persona string in the returned UA. S32: `ab` was aliased to `agent-browser --cdp 9333` while cuttle served 9222 - any habitual use would have silently driven a different browser with no error. S01: the agent opened 'a fresh isolated browser session' outside cuttle for a second identity and the user had to ask 'are you using cuttle? or some magic stuff yourslef?' before it learned that a second identity is `cuttle up --name`.
clustered_issues.root_cause: Port reachability is treated as identity. Nothing stamps which cuttle instance and seed a driver session is on, and nothing makes 'am I attached to cuttle?' answerable.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: A stable instance identity (id, arch, persona, start time) on the HTTP surface that any consumer can assert against, and `cuttle status` listing attached driver sessions - plus the 'second identity = second named instance' recipe at the top of the briefing.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~25 calls, one voided probe run, and one whole detour into a non-cuttle browser.

clustered_issues.issue: Daemon and Chrome death is invisible to attached clients: a panic surfaces as a bare ECONNREFUSED or a 502 whose body parses as success, a page disappearing carries no attribution, and `cuttle status`'s log tail is 20 lines of dbus noise.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S03 shipped two releases carrying a crash because the harness reported 9/10 green while the daemon it was driving had died: 'My earlier confirmed fixed was wrong: I checked at 23:49, and the daemon panicked at 23:51:20, after the harness finished' - the panic (`chromedp.NewContext.func1() chromedp.go:199`) was found only by reading pod exit state. S07 lost a filled wizard step to 'Daemon process exited with code 1 [PlaywrightError: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9222]' and `cuttle status`'s entire 'last 20 log lines' window was repeats of '[ERROR:dbus/bus.cc:405] Failed to connect to the bus'. S12 spent hours and three subagents on 'Target page, context or browser has been closed' while 'Cuttle's own logs show the a link-aggregator site Chromes are not crashing - clean disconnected + state captured ~2s after connect'; separately, 'cuttle answers a dead Chrome with a 502 whose body is valid JSON, so it degrades to chrome ?, unknown persona instead of naming the failure.'
clustered_issues.root_cause: cuttle has no health or liveness surface a driving agent can poll, no per-teardown attribution (client closeTarget vs transport drop vs idle reap vs crash), a status log tail biased toward benign Chromium noise, and error responses shaped identically to success.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle status` reporting daemon uptime, restart/panic count with stack, and last-capture outcomes; per-page teardown attribution surfaced in the CDP error path; error bodies that cannot be parsed as the success shape; and a log tail biased toward panic/fatal/exit lines.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~100 calls, hours of investigation across three subagents in one session, two releases shipped with a live crash, and one false green.

clustered_issues.issue: `playwright-cli attach` routinely reports success and an error in the same output, so the very first command of a session leaves the agent unsure whether it is attached.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest:
S06's first browser call: '### Session `default` created, attached to `http://127.0.0.1:9222`.
Run commands with: playwright-cli --s=default <command>

### Error
Error: Target page, context or browser has been closed'. S25 hit the identical output and re-attached blind to find out. In S06 the subsequent tab-list showed a healthy browser with `- 1: [](about:blank)` between the user's two real tabs, and the agent re-attached defensively three more times over the session purely from distrust.
clustered_issues.root_cause: The driver's attach appears to bind to cuttle's immortal keep-alive about:blank target and find it unusable. That target also occupies a tab ordinal, shifting every index after it.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Hide or mark the keep-alive target so drivers skip it as the default page, or guarantee a live attachable target before `up` returns; failing that, state in SKILL.md that this specific error on attach is benign.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~8 calls of defensive re-attaching.

clustered_issues.issue: A bare `timeout` is indistinguishable from a bot wall, a structurally unrenderable target, or a slow-but-viable page - so one bad fetch becomes a retry loop and version comparisons produce noise reported as improvement.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S44: 'The browser farm can't render a Docs editor inside the budget... Two 25s attempts -> browser tier timed out x2 -> 51s -> outcome: timeout' and Loki showed a cloud document suite at 5 attempts / 0 successes over 30 days, '3 were a user on 2026-08-11 hitting the same doc - and notably their third try was /export?format=txt, which also failed... because a browser navigating to a text/plain download produces nothing.' S03: `web:a large social network` FAIL `outcome=timeout` 155s, reproduced four times across three environments before it could be attributed as pre-existing; a short-video platform flipped pass/fail across runs and an improvement was reported then retracted. S12's subagent: 'A genuine silent challenge would look identical.'
clustered_issues.root_cause: The render path returns a single opaque outcome with no forensics attached, and there is no per-attempt budget or early abort when an engine is provably doomed.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Attach cheap forensics to any navigation timeout - last committed URL, document.title, bytes/text extracted, content-type, challenge-sentinel match - and a caller-settable per-attempt budget with an abort when the remaining budget cannot cover a render.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~30 calls across four full matrix runs, plus repeated user-facing retry loops.

clustered_issues.issue: Local (arm64/qemu) and production (amd64) cuttle diverge on architecture, persona, memory and timeouts with nothing surfacing the difference, so the pages that most need testing cannot be tested locally at all.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S03: a large e-commerce site 'exceeds page.goto's 45s timeout before it ever gets to the anti-bot check', a short-video platform/a large social network 'blow the web tier's 25s render budget'; the human, not the agent, unblocked it - 'can you do run on ssh <remote-host> for example then to check?' - and native measurement showed 'identity:us took 2.5s on <remote-host> vs 9.2s locally'. The same session found the gate meant to catch this was itself misconfigured: 'the canary was provisioned at half of prod's memory, and a disk-backed emptyDir for /dev/shm where prod has a tmpfs.'
