S12 then found a 'canary-only, blame qemu' comment had been covering a permanent a large social network failure on production-identical amd64 for months.
clustered_issues.root_cause: The image is multi-arch, the arch selects the stealth persona, and the render budget is a fixed constant that emulation silently blows through - so a local failure is indistinguishable from a real one and stale in-repo explanations go unchallenged.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Warn loudly at startup when running translated ('render budgets are not meaningful here'), name the native-arm64 image as the local-dev path, and make the render budget configurable per invocation.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~15 wasted local runs plus months of a permanently-red gate nobody read.

clustered_issues.issue: A plain discovery GET to /json/version with no ?fingerprint= launches the reserved __default__ seed - a real headed Chrome with direct unproxied egress - which is never reaped because no CDP connection arms the idle reaper.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S12, review finding then confirmed live: 'describeFarm() sends no ?fingerprint=, so cuttle launches the reserved __default__ seed - a real headed Chrome with direct, unproxied egress - and because a discovery-only GET never opens a CDP connection, the idle reaper is never armed, so it is never reaped. Confirmed live: /data/__default__ is running in the local container right now.' Worst on the canary, which the same change had just tuned to mirror prod memory exactly, then silently added an unaccounted ~500MB Chrome to.
clustered_issues.root_cause: Metadata discovery and browser provisioning share an endpoint, and reaper arming is tied to CDP connect rather than to spawn.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Serve /json/version metadata without spawning a seed (or arm the reaper on spawn, or refuse __default__ for discovery), plus a cheap 'describe farm' endpoint that costs no browser.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~4 calls, but a permanent resource and egress leak per probing consumer.

clustered_issues.issue: cuttle's CDP surface is unauthenticated with no bind restriction, and was reachable by unauthenticated callers on the deployment network.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S44, verified in a deployed environment: `glim_web_fetch("http://<deployment-host>:9222/json/version")` -> 200, returning the cuttle webSocketDebuggerUrl. The agent's commit note: 'CDP's HTTP endpoints (/json/new, /json/list) manipulate the browser farm.' Discovered only because an unrelated SSRF audit went looking.
clustered_issues.root_cause: No token, no allowlist, no bind-scope default, and no way for an operator to see which interface the CDP port is bound to.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: A shared-secret/bearer token on the CDP HTTP+WS surface, loopback-only binding by default with an explicit opt-in to listen wider, and bind scope reported in `cuttle status`.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~15 calls for the fix arc, but the exposure had been live indefinitely.

clustered_issues.issue: Kubernetes injects `CUTTLE_PORT=tcp://<cluster-ip>:9222` for a Service named `cuttle`, which cuttle parses as its own --port and exits 1 - the most obvious deployment name poisons its own config.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S12: 'The new cuttle pod is in CrashLoopBackOff and the old daemon pod is already gone - the browser farm is down.' Root cause: 'Kubernetes injects legacy Docker-link env vars for every Service in the namespace: naming the Service cuttle makes k8s inject CUTTLE_PORT=tcp://<cluster-ip>:9222, which collides with cuttle's own --port config var.' And: 'helmfile template could never catch this; it's a runtime injection.'
clustered_issues.root_cause: cuttle's env-var config namespace (CUTTLE_*) is exactly the namespace Kubernetes reserves for service links, and cuttle accepts a `tcp://host:port` value as a port without complaint.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Reject or ignore a CUTTLE_PORT whose value looks like `tcp://host:port` (unambiguously a service link) and say so in a startup log line; warn in the container docs.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~10 calls plus a ~4-minute production outage.

clustered_issues.issue: Window, viewport and spoofed screen geometry are incoherent and unowned: drivers hardcode a viewport over cuttle's careful sizing, the window does not match the VNC framebuffer, a convenience `resize` silently breaks the fingerprint, and clicks below the fold no-op with no error.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S12's audit measured it end to end: 'innerWidth (1920, hardcoded by cloakbrowser's DEFAULT_VIEWPORT and again by scrapling) exceeds both outerWidth and screen.width on every render... macOS is incoherent on 5/5 of cuttle's screen pool, Windows on 3/4 - so prod is quietly incoherent ~75% of the time too.' S03 measured the other direction on attach: 'outer=2560x1392 inner=780x403', and found http.go:196 prefixes every unknown query param as --fingerprint-<key>= so --window-size can never actually be passed. S02 shows the agent-facing cost: 'Click landed off-screen (y=1035 vs 959 viewport)... the coordinate click silently does nothing - calendar closes, value unchanged, no error.' S04 issued one `resize 1440 900` for nicer screenshots and ran every subsequent logged-in write under it.
clustered_issues.root_cause: Three different numbers (spoofed screen, OS window, driver viewport) are set by three different layers, none of which can see the others, and cuttle neither clamps nor warns.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Detect and clamp or loudly warn when a client's viewport/device-metrics override contradicts the seed's spoofed screen; report window/viewport/framebuffer geometry in `cuttle status`; and auto-scroll-into-view before coordinate clicks.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~25 calls plus a silent, systematic stealth regression on ~75% of production renders.

clustered_issues.issue: The humanizer's own pre-click probes ran in the main world at up to ~17 evaluates per click - the anti-detection feature was itself detectable.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S16: humanize.go:693 sent Runtime.evaluate with no contextId. Measured on live containers: 0.11.3 leaked 2 observable main-world probes per click, 0.11.4 leaks 0. The upstream project had already shipped a release for the same class: 'Fix humanize=True triggering invisible CAPTCHA challenges during clicks. Humanized pre-click checks are now stealth-safe.'
clustered_issues.root_cause: Pre-click state probes were issued into the page's own JS context, observable to any page that watches for injected evaluation.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Fixed in 0.11.4 (cached Page.createIsolatedWorld per session, contextId on every probe). The general lesson: any daemon-side probing of the page needs an isolated world by construction, and a test should assert zero main-world evaluates per humanized action.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: Unknown, but plausibly the cause of captcha escalations agents then spent turns fighting.

clustered_issues.issue: Driver verb discovery happens by trial and error mid-task: unknown commands answer with a full usage dump and no 'did you mean', and the `cuttle up` briefing teaches attachment but not a single page verb.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: Three different wrong tab verbs in three sessions - `new-tab` (S23), `tabs` (S26), `navigate` (S27) - each answered with a 40-line usage block. Also `nav` twice, `resize`, `viewport`, `close-session`, and `--path=` instead of `--filename` (S09). S04 interleaved `playwright-cli --help 2>&1 | grep -iE "^  (goto|open|nav|tab)"` with real work on a live account. S17's guessed `tabs` verb produced nothing at all, so the agent could not tell 'no tabs' from 'no such command'.
clustered_issues.root_cause: The briefing points at each driver's docs command as an optional link rather than inlining the 6-8 verbs every session needs, and driver errors do not name that docs command.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Inline a most-used verb cheat (goto, snapshot, find, click, fill, upload, screenshot, tab-*) per driver in the `cuttle up` briefing, and have unknown-command errors point at the driver's own docs command.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~35 calls plus repeated large help dumps consuming context.

clustered_issues.issue: cuttle's embedded SKILL.md carried factually false claims about the daemon's own behaviour, and agents read them and acted on them.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S16: 'Two stale items in the skill itself: internal/cli/SKILL.md:200 claims off-centre clicks (the code removed that at humanize.go:398-403), and it says typing is rewritten into human-paced motion when fill on both drivers goes through Input.insertText, which the humanizer never sees.' S02's agent wrote a false claim about cuttle into the user's own repo and had to retract it: 'That was the whole bug - a background tab, not a cuttle limitation. Let me correct the playbook immediately.' S03 found cuttle's source comment claiming a caller could pass --window-size when http.go:196 makes it impossible.
clustered_issues.root_cause: SKILL.md is //go:embed'ed and therefore shipped behaviour, but nothing keeps its behavioural claims under test against the daemon's code paths.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: A test asserting SKILL.md's behavioural claims against the daemon (keystroke counts on fill, click offsets, flag pass-through), so docs drift cannot land silently.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: At least one wrong stealth decision in a live session and one false claim persisted into a user's repo.

clustered_issues.issue: The operational facts that actually decide success live nowhere durable, so every session rediscovers the same mechanics and then writes a private cuttle playbook into the user's own repo - three different users' repos now carry hand-rolled cuttle documentation.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: The same four driver mechanics were re-derived independently in at least five sessions: run-code is Node not the page, run-code needs an `async page => {}` wrapper, long text needs insertText, click sometimes needs raw mouse coordinates. S10 wrote them into `pjs/career/docs/SCAM_REPORTING.md` under a heading 'Driving these forms with cuttle' - a scam-reporting playbook now carrying cuttle's driver documentation. S01 wrote a 34-line block into `pjs/finances/CLAUDE.md`; S02 rewrote `tools/a professional social network-access/CLAUDE.md` with a 'three time-wasters' section. The humans said it directly: 'have you checked full skills/docs of both tools? could it be that we are just not using them in the most efficient way they could be used and doing some dumb shit instead?' (S07, agent's own answer: 'Roughly 12-15 of my ~30 browser calls were avoidable') and 'read cuttle's skill and check full playwright-cli skill / you should be able to do that yourself!' (S08). S28 truncated the briefing to `tail -2` to save context, discarding the routing rules entirely.
clustered_issues.root_cause: The briefing names drivers and attach commands; the load-bearing facts (read the driver's full reference first, locators pierce shadow DOM and eval does not, never dispatchEvent through cuttle, the secrets file binds at attach, host paths are invisible to the browser, humanized input is slow by design, refs are single-use, where driver scratch state lands) are carried by neither the briefing nor SKILL.md.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Move the handful of operational rules into the embedded SKILL.md and a short, stable `cuttle up` briefing - short enough that agents stop truncating it - with the full guide behind `cuttle skill`.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: By one agent's own count, 12-15 of ~30 browser calls in a single session; corpus-wide the largest single lever after visibility.

clustered_issues.issue: There is no place to persist per-site knowledge, so recurring authenticated jobs are re-derived from scratch every run and users end up demanding hand-written recipes in their own repos.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S29's user: 'why each time it takes so much time for you to just fetch data and compare it with ... could you update pjs/career/CLAUDE.md so that when i ask you to check for new missions on a freelance marketplace - it would be the straightforward workflow for you without erroring on each step?' The agent's five listed causes were four browser/driver frictions. S16 quantified the payoff: 'codifying the a freelance marketplace check into 4 commands + a baseline TSV took a recurring job from 24 calls / 11.6 min to 2 calls / 47s.' Two other sessions wrote a consumer banking web app and a professional social network recipes only after paying full price.
clustered_issues.root_cause: cuttle has a `context` concept but nothing carries a per-site playbook alongside a seed, so the discovery cost of every authenticated dashboard is paid on every visit by every session.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Per-seed/per-site recipes attached to a cuttle context (or at minimum a documented convention and location), so a working sequence becomes a durable asset instead of a one-off discovery.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~22 avoidable calls per recurring run, in a corpus dominated by recurring authenticated checks.

clustered_issues.issue: Inline JS in a shell argument is broken in every driver, so agents independently invent the same heredoc-to-file workaround - roughly 30 throwaway .js files across the window, some written into the user's repo.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S06 wrote 21 of its 40 run-code calls to a file because nested quoting could not survive `page.locator('button:has(use[href=\"...\"])')`; S05 wrote /tmp/inspect3.js, /tmp/usercap.js, /tmp/userhtml.js and more; a separate agent-browser session had regex flags mangled by escaping ('✗ Evaluation error: SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression flags') and then wrote nine .js files. S22's heredoc plumbing failed with a misleading `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')'` plus an unrelated 'Shell cwd was reset' line. S20 had to drop `const` and arrow functions from an eval to survive three layers of quoting.
clustered_issues.root_cause: The documented invocation style passes JavaScript as a shell argument, which fails on regex, nested quotes and multi-line code - and the resulting error names a JS token rather than the plumbing.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Document the write-to-file-then-`--filename` pattern as the default for anything longer than one expression (with a scratchpad path convention), and offer `cuttle eval --file` so the driver-specific step disappears.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~10 calls lost to quoting errors plus ~30 file writes.

clustered_issues.issue: Driver output is not a machine-readable contract - `--raw` returns double-JSON-encoded values and mixes progress chatter and harness noise with the payload - so shell-side parsing breaks repeatedly.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S29: `jq: error (at board.json:1): Cannot index string with string ("data")` - the raw body was `"{\"data\":[{\"mid\":..."` - and the fix (`jq -r .` first) had to be re-applied to four separate fetches and then written into CLAUDE.md as gotcha #1 with the note 'Nothing in CLAUDE.md warns about it.' S07 lost two calls to `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError` from `| tail -2 | python3 -c "json.loads(json.loads(...))"` because even --raw output carries ANSI-dim '- fonts loaded' lines and an appended 'Shell cwd was reset'. S25 hit three `jq: parse error: Invalid numeric literal` in one session.
clustered_issues.root_cause: No stated output contract per verb; diagnostics and payload share stdout and the encoding depth varies.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Document the exact output contract per verb, or provide a thin `cuttle exec`/`cuttle eval --json` wrapper that emits only the JSON payload on stdout and diagnostics on stderr.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~15 calls of broken pipelines and re-runs.

clustered_issues.issue: Driver scratch state (snapshots, console logs, screenshots, session dirs) is written cwd-relative into whatever repo the agent is working in - it got 3,100 lines committed once and hard-failed every command another time.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S02: 'my earlier .gitignore negation for the a professional social network export was broad enough to re-admit playwright-cli's scratch state, so a first commit swept in ~3,100 lines of console logs and page snapshots.' S18: a stale zero-byte `.playwright-cli` file in a repo root made every driver command fail with `Error: EEXIST: file already exists, mkdir '~/Projects/pond/.playwright-cli'` - and the failing command had already opened a tab. S05 prefixed all 183 calls with `cd <scratchpad> &&` because the shell resets cwd; S10 had to run a three-way `ls -t`/`find -newermt` search to locate a screenshot it had just taken.
clustered_issues.root_cause: The driver owns artifact placement and defaults to the current working directory, which cuttle's briefing never mentions; cuttle owns no artifact location of its own.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: cuttle owns a stable per-session artifact directory (outside any git working tree) and prints absolute paths; the briefing states where each driver writes scratch state.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~15 calls plus one polluted git commit and one fully-blocked session start.

clustered_issues.issue: cuttle is not reached for when it should be: agents default to fetch/cached research on pages the user has a live login for, and the human has to say the word 'cuttle' before the browser is considered.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S30 researched a logged-in-only a professional social network profile from a stale cached public snapshot and reported it as current; the user pushed twice - 'Are you sure that you checked the correct profile?' then 'check hher profile with cuttle' - before the agent ran `which cuttle`. S25: 'try getting those notion pages content through cuttle', sent only after glim_web_fetch timed out on both Notion URLs. S32 needed three discovery calls after the human said 'could you also use cuttle'. A separate session hit a hard login wall ('Privy needs an emailed code'), gave up on the real dashboard, verified against a throwaway stub route, shipped, and told the user 'One thing left for you, since I can't log in' - having never loaded cuttle at all.
clustered_issues.root_cause: Skill triggering keys on the word 'browser' rather than on the intents that actually need cuttle (read this page behind a login; a fetch returned a JS shell or a login wall or timed out).
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Trigger the skill on 'read/open this page' intents and state the escalation rule explicitly in the briefing: any fetch that returns a JS shell, a login wall, or a timeout is a cuttle job - plus `cuttle status` listing which origins the profile currently holds sessions for.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~15 calls plus one confidently-wrong research answer and one shipped feature never verified against the real dashboard.

clustered_issues.issue: Anti-bot challenge type is not detectable, so the agent clicked at an invisible reCAPTCHA badge that had nothing to click and burned a minute of sleeps - on cuttle's own core territory.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S08: two frameLocator attempts returned only '- waiting for locator(iframe[src*="recaptcha/api2/anchor"]).contentFrame().locator(#recaptcha-anchor)' and nothing else; the agent then ran `mousemove 1392 636; mousedown; mouseup; sleep 8` returning `{"tokenLen":0,"challengeVisible":false}`, plus a 12-iteration polling loop and a `sleep 25`, before concluding: 'That's the invisible reCAPTCHA badge, not a checkbox - it mints the token on submit. So nothing to click.'
clustered_issues.root_cause: No verb or recipe reports which challenge is present (reCAPTCHA v2 checkbox / v3 / invisible badge / Turnstile / image captcha) or whether it needs interaction, and the cross-origin frame timeouts say nothing useful.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: `cuttle challenge detect` (or a documented SKILL.md recipe) reporting challenge type and whether interaction is required - plus a scaled element capture so an image captcha is legible in one call rather than a screenshot-plus-PIL pipeline.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~10 calls and ~1 minute of sleeps.

clustered_issues.issue: Irreversible outward actions from a logged-in account have no per-action confirmation gate, and the human's tolerance for them varies sharply.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S04 clicked Delete and then 'Yes, delete' on the user's live resume with only a local backup as mitigation; the user's next message was 'i just updated the resume on resume tab myself'. S12's session produced the sharpest reaction in the corpus - 'stop stop stop! no issue creation anywhere! what are you doing! i never allowed that!' - while another session's user said 'submit all of them' about equivalent form submits.
clustered_issues.root_cause: Plan-level agreement is treated as authorization for each outward act. Nothing in cuttle or the skill marks destructive affordances (delete/remove/deactivate/submit) on a live account as requiring a fresh confirmation or a viewer handoff.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: SKILL.md names destructive affordances on live accounts as a handoff trigger (park the page, print the viewer URL, ask), and any cuttle verb that performs an irreversible outward action requires per-action confirmation rather than a plan-level agreement.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~10 calls plus two user interventions, one of them an interrupt.

clustered_issues.issue: The containerized browser reports only partial WebAuthn/passkey support, so the auth flow most accounts are moving to is unusable and every sudo/2FA wall degrades to a device tap or a TOTP the agent should not handle.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S18: 'I picked GitHub Mobile over the passkey (the container browser reports only partial passkey support) and over the authenticator app (that would mean you reading a TOTP code into the transcript).' The resulting handoff stalled the whole workstream ~36 hours.
clustered_issues.root_cause: WebAuthn status in cuttle's Chromium is undocumented, so agents probe it and then route around it.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Document cuttle's WebAuthn status explicitly in SKILL.md, and consider a virtual-authenticator or host-passkey bridge for the handoff path.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: Avoided-path cost rather than retries; contributed to a ~36h stall.

clustered_issues.issue: Container contract changes shipped with no compatibility error: the cuttleserve shim was removed and CLOAKBROWSER_BINARY_PATH stopped being read, silently, leaving three call sites that would not start.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S03: 'The /usr/local/bin/cuttleserve shim is gone (image cmd is `cuttle serve`) and CLOAKBROWSER_BINARY_PATH is no longer read (now CUTTLE_BROWSER_BINARY, baked to /opt/browser/chrome). Our compose.yml:47 and helmfile.yaml.gotmpl:137 both still say cuttleserve - the container would not start.' The same stale contract was hardcoded in scripts/cuttle-canary.sh and found only by reading the script.
clustered_issues.root_cause: Removed entrypoints and env vars are ignored rather than diagnosed, so a stale consumer fails at container start with no message naming the change.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: A one-release deprecation shim that starts and prints 'cuttleserve is gone, use `cuttle serve`', and an entrypoint warning on any recognized-but-removed env var.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: ~6 calls of grepping call sites.

clustered_issues.issue: cuttle's resource footprint is a live landmine that constrains deployment and development, with no guard against a second instance landing on the same host.
clustered_issues.evidence_digest: S44 had to encode a do-not-do-this into a handoff plan: never rename the helm release because 'helmfile won't uninstall a vanished release and you'd end up with a second 6Gi farm on the ~6.9Gi browser node (the 2026-06-12 OOM)'. A separate local performance investigation measured the cuttle container at 26-32% of a host core - roughly two-thirds of all OrbStack CPU - during unrelated work.
clustered_issues.root_cause: Per-seed memory cost is undocumented and nothing detects a second cuttle already holding the profile dir or port on the same host.
clustered_issues.capability_gap: Document per-seed memory cost in the briefing, and have the daemon refuse or loudly warn when another cuttle already holds the profile dir or port rather than letting a second farm take the node down.
clustered_issues.estimated_agent_cost: No direct call cost; one node lost to OOM historically.

blind_spots:
Nine structural blind spots, all of which bias this ranking in the same direction - toward things agents tried and away from things that were never attempted or never observed.

1. The human half of the loop is unrecorded. cuttle's flagship handoff is one X display (`Xvnc :99 -geometry 1920x1080`, openbox, -AlwaysShared, no auth) shared by every seed's Chrome. Nothing that happens in that room is logged: keystrokes, tab closes, dialog dismissals, a cookie banner cleared, a password typed into the wrong seed's window. The corpus contains only the fraction the human narrated afterwards, and those are the angry cases ("i entered creds myself", "i did mouse drag myself"). The larger quiet class is the human silently unblocking something and the agent's next command simply working - which every transcript scores as a cuttle success. Every apparent success rate here is inflated by an unknown amount of unrecorded human labor, always in the same direction.

2. Non-attempts leave no residue. A capability with a broken verb produces an error, a retry ladder, and a cluster. A capability with no verb and no doc line produces nothing. S07's upload gap surfaced only because the human happened to ask "wasn't there any place in form to submit docs?"; without that question it reads as a clean session. Missing surface, agent ignorance of existing surface, and "not needed" are indistinguishable in a transcript. Issues 6, 7, 18, 24, 25, 26 and 27 are all partly recovered from this dark region and are therefore certainly under-ranked, not over-ranked.

3. Stealth outcomes are the one thing cuttle exists for and the one thing a transcript can never contain. No site announces a raised risk score, a degraded page, a shadowban, or a challenge queued for three visits from now. The corpus can count 185 isTrusted:false clicks and the ~75% of renders where the driver's hardcoded 1920 viewport exceeds the seed's spoofed screen.width; it cannot observe one consequence of either. The 0.11.3 main-world probe leak is the proof: for that release's whole life it emitted observable evaluates on every click, and the cost landed in transcripts as "a captcha appeared and the agent fought it for ten calls," filed against the site. Whole categories of cuttle-caused failure are sitting in this corpus mislabeled as site behaviour.

4. Transcript-mined root causes are agents' beliefs, and about cuttle's internals those beliefs are demonstrably wrong. The background-tab bug wore four disguises for two weeks; S02 published "cuttle's Chromium never fires the lazy RSC requests" before finding document.hidden. Sharpest case: Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled makes hasFocus() return true, so the daemon actively falsifies the diagnostic the agent reaches for, and the agent's confidently wrong conclusion is then mined as evidence. Anything an agent never suspected cuttle for is filed elsewhere permanently.

5. Abandonment reads as competence. Three font-loading timeouts and S04 stops taking screenshots for the rest of the session; two actionability timeouts and a session never uses a high-level verb again; S05 prefixes all 183 calls with `cd <scratchpad>`. Giving up is one line; what the agent would have done with a working primitive is unwritten. Worse, the cost then migrates out of transcripts entirely - once "ASSUME LOGGED OUT" and "never a secret in fill or run-code" are written into the human's own CLAUDE.md, the friction is paid on every future run while generating no new evidence forever.

6. Silent-wrong-answer sessions look identical to correct ones. 15 sessions used cuttle as an authenticated cookie jar and dispatched zero input events; three sent zero clicks. If the seed's server session had expired, a lazy loader never fired because the tab was backgrounded, or an in-page fetch hit different cookie semantics than the real request, the output is still shaped correctly. The corpus has exactly one datapoint on this class - the tax figure the human caught by eye - and it is a datapoint about that human's checking habits, not about the error rate. A transcript audit has no ground truth outside the transcript and cannot grade correctness.

7. Losses that cross a session boundary have no owner. The cookie-capture defect (default context only, empty capture overwrites good snapshot, profile then deleted) was found by source review, not by any session failing, because the consequence lands next week in a different session where the agent narrates a re-login as routine. Same for the never-reaped __default__ seed and for the daemon panicking after a harness finished green. The daemon has the timeline; the transcripts have fragments on either side of a gap.

8. The multi-client collision base rate is unknowable. S05 and S06 were caught only because both narrated confusion in the same minute against the same container. With no attached-client list and no ownership, the ordinary collision is one weird result - a click that did nothing, a tab that vanished - retried and attributed to the page. One loud pair surfaced; the quiet ones are by construction indistinguishable from flaky sites.

9. Felt cost is not call count, and never-delegated tasks are invisible. A person watching the framebuffer while the agent removes and re-adds thirty skill chips at ~0.5s/click and ~130ms/char on their own live profile experiences five minutes of visible slow typing into a real account plus the moment where the next click might be Delete. The corpus contains one interrupt; every near-interrupt and every task the human simply did himself (the slider form, the passkey login, the upload) leaves nothing behind, and 14 days of silence on those reads as 14 days without problems.

Two things that genuinely cannot be evidenced from this corpus and are therefore excluded from the ranking rather than ranked low: (a) any measurement of cuttle's actual detection rate on real anti-bot systems - the only honest instrument is an external bench, not transcripts; (b) any baseline of what a good session looks like, because nobody clustered successes - the single clean interaction in the batch is flagged in-line in S06 ("the one browser interaction in either session that went cleanly", the viewer handoff) and appears in no cluster, so every severity here is measured against an unstated ideal.
